title: ai-cli-utils project-registry writer omits path field, reproduces SW-890 outage class
description:
Two write sites in src/ai_cli/config.py append [[projects]] stanzas to sergei.toml (or the resolved main-project registry file) with name/task_prefix/type/active but never write path, even though the full project directory path is in scope at both call sites. sergei.toml's own guard comment marks path as REQUIRED alongside name -- a missing path is the exact SW-890 failure class that crashed the ai-core MCP startup and froze the whole memory substrate for months. Found live: ai-harness-lite and nyc-events stanzas in sergei.toml were missing path, hand-fixed in a separate commit (7265d840), but the generator that produced them is still broken and will reproduce this on the next unregistered-project prompt.

Site 1: _append_projects_entry, src/ai_cli/config.py:575-581 -- builds the entry f-string from root (a full Path) and prefix, but never interpolates path = "{root}". Called by _prompt_and_persist_prefix (config.py:630-642), the last tier of resolve_project_prefix (config.py:645), triggered when ai c/session launch needs a task prefix for an unregistered project and prompts interactively. Write target resolves via _registry_write_target (config.py:589-601) -> _get_project_registry_path (config.py:782-789) -> main_dir / f"{name}.toml", i.e. sergei.toml when main_project = sergei.

Site 2: inline in validate_registry_completeness, src/ai_cli/config.py:911-913 -- appends entries via a plain file .write() in a loop, also omitting path even though the scanning loop just above (config.py:872-877) iterates projects_dir.iterdir() and has the directory d (the full path) in scope. Runs from main.py:1761-1767, invoked automatically before an unqualified ai c session launch, prompting per unregistered directory found under projects_dir.

Fix: interpolate path = "{root}" (site 1) and path = "{d}" (site 2, normalized consistently with how other entries in sergei.toml write path, e.g. ~/projects/<name> vs an absolute path -- check existing convention) into both entry-writing f-strings/write calls, so every newly-registered project stanza carries path from the moment it's created.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: _append_projects_entry (config.py:575-581) writes a path field for the new [[projects]] entry, derived from the root argument already in scope. AC-2: the inline entry-writer in validate_registry_completeness (config.py:911-913) writes a path field for each new entry, derived from d already in scope in the loop above. AC-3: the written path value follows the same normalization convention as existing sergei.toml entries (spot-check: does the registry use ~/projects/<name> or an absolute path -- match it, don't introduce a third convention). AC-4: a regression test exists for both write sites asserting the written TOML text/parsed entry contains a non-empty path field. AC-5 (failure-path): a test confirms that if root/d cannot be resolved to a usable path, the function fails loudly (matching the file's own documented behavior of load_config skipping-with-a-loud-error on a missing path) rather than silently writing an empty or malformed path value.
close_reason: Fixed and landed on origin/main at b19ad966. _append_projects_entry (site 1) now normalizes to ~/projects/<name> when under home, else absolute, and raises ProjectPrefixError before writing if the path doesn't resolve; validate_registry_completeness's inline writer (site 2) now threads the scanned Path through instead of only keeping the name string. Verified: 94 focused + full suite 2312 passed / 0 failed in the real environment, ruff clean. Delegated to Codex implement (gpt-5.6-terra, medium effort, session bdupu690z).

title: Fix stranded-autostash: ai update discards a lying exit code and latches the repo behind forever

comments.author: T
comments.text:
Shipped in ai-cli-utils 5cacff5 + cda724f (branch worktree-aih443-shapeb, merged to main).

MECHANISM: `git pull --rebase --autostash` exits 0 when its automatic stash pop conflicts. Measured on git 2.55.0 (macOS) and 2.43.0 (Linux), fast-forward and rebasing pulls alike. Negative control on the same harness: a rebase-BODY conflict exits 1, so the harness can see failure.

CALLERS (ours): main.py _do_update_or_deploy did not bind the code at all (check=False) and its conflict scan only read src/**/*.py — the live conflict was in .gitignore. The ai c N worktree launch gated on returncode != 0, which never fires.

LATCH: once conflicted, later pulls exit 128 and were also discarded. Filed separately as AI-CLI-135.

FIX: pull_rebase_autostash() measures repo state either side of the pull (new unmerged paths, new stash ids, no operation in progress) instead of trusting the exit code.

PROOF: old gate MISSED and new guard CAUGHT the identical genuine conflict; disabling either clause turns the regression tests red; disabling the ai update branch makes it exit 0 and install from the conflicted checkout.

TESTS: 1867 -> 1887 passed, 7 skipped.

Cross-family review by Codex found 6 issues, all real, all fixed in cda724f — including one HIGH where the pre-existing cleanup would have destroyed a user's in-progress conflict resolution, and one HIGH where the bug doc leaked a routable host into a PUBLIC repo.

REMOTE HOST: un-stranded, 0 behind, clean index. All four stashes left INTACT — see AI-CLI-136.

title: quota scrape orphans CC auto-update downloads, 8 GB/day
description: ai quota scrape (cron */10) launches claude in a throwaway tmux session and unconditionally kills it in the finally block (quota.py:429-434) ~15s later. CC's background auto-updater has by then started downloading the new version into ~/.cache/claude/staging/VER.PID.MS/claude; the kill truncates it mid-write and nobody ever reaps the partial. Hetzner box: 402 entries, 23 GB, 400 of them landing exactly on cron minutes. Fix: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 in the scrape session + a bounded reaper.

title: DONE 2026-07-20: test suite can no longer leak real tmux/agent sessions
description: `[P0]` `[AI-CLI-117]` **DONE 2026-07-20: test suite can no longer leak real tmux/agent sessions** — Root cause of AI-CLI-116's `c-hm-1`/`g-myproject-1` incident was three local-project launch tests that mocked final `os.execvp` but let earlier `subprocess.run(["tmux", ...])` calls execute. Added explicit subprocess mocks and test-only `pytest-leak-guard-` session names, plus an autouse process guard that loudly rejects unmocked `tmux`, `claude`, `gemini`, or `direnv` calls through `run`, `Popen`, or `execvp`; session teardown removes only names with that test prefix. Eight focused regression tests cover the guard, patch layering, cleanup, and affected launch paths. Driver review (Claude, post-Codex-implementation) initially over-narrowed the `real_tmux` marker's allowance to `subprocess.run` only, which broke the isolated-socket integration suite — `libtmux` uses `subprocess.Popen` internally for every tmux command against that socket. Corrected: `run`/`Popen` both honor the marker (needed for the isolated-socket teardown + libtmux's own calls), `execvp` never does (no test needs a real `execvp("tmux", ...)`, and letting one through would silently replace the pytest worker instead of failing loudly). Verified: full suite 1853 passed, 0 skipped, and `tmux list-sessions` diffed byte-identical before/after the run — the actual acceptance check Codex's own sandbox couldn't perform (no tmux socket access there). Related: AI-CLI-116 (detection/cleanup for the original leaked sessions), AI-CLI-97 (prior subprocess isolation guard pattern).

title: `[AI-CLI-113]`'s worktree-`.envrc` auto-allow never actually fires — `direnv status --json`'s `allowed` field is not a reliable trust signal
description: `[P0]` `[AI-CLI-114]` **`[AI-CLI-113]`'s worktree-`.envrc` auto-allow never actually fires — `direnv status --json`'s `allowed` field is not a reliable trust signal** — Root cause: `state.foundRC.allowed` did not reflect whether direnv could execute the repository `.envrc`, so the root trust guard returned before auto-allowing an identical worktree file. Fixed: probe the worktree with `direnv exec <worktree> true` first and return when already usable; only after a failure probe the root with the same command, then allow only a byte-identical worktree `.envrc`. The generated launcher now recognizes the literal blocked error from that failed `direnv exec` stderr rather than querying status JSON. The targeted-launch registry symptom remains non-reproducible; a `cli()` regression with a real registry TOML and unregistered directory verifies discovery is never called for a named launch. README clarifies the executable-root trust policy. 5 new/updated regression tests; 1837 tests collected, focused session/main suite 183 passed; ruff clean on touched Python files. Related: `[AI-CLI-113]`, `[AI-CLI-79]`.

title: Bug: auto-restart falls back to shell on a blocked worktree `.envrc`, then `ai c` relaunch hangs on an unrelated unregistered-project prompt
description: `[P0]` `[AI-CLI-113]` **Bug: auto-restart falls back to shell on a blocked worktree `.envrc`, then `ai c` relaunch hangs on an unrelated unregistered-project prompt** — Root cause: Git checks a tracked `.envrc` into a new worktree without creating direnv's path-specific approval, while every launch eagerly scanned and interactively synced all projects before resolving a named target. Fixed: worktree creation auto-allows only a byte-identical `.envrc` whose repository-root source is already approved; the auto-restart wrapper detects a blocked `.envrc` and prints the precise recovery command; named/explicit-project launches skip unrelated registry discovery. Registry prompts now write atomically and propagate Ctrl-C immediately; `cli()` gained a top-level `KeyboardInterrupt` handler (Click's `standalone_mode=False` doesn't convert a raw Ctrl-C from `input()` into `click.exceptions.Abort` on its own, so without this a stray interrupt printed a Python traceback instead of exiting cleanly). README documents the trust and discovery policy. Driver review (Claude, post-Codex-implementation) found and fixed one stale test (`test_cli.py::TestCliRegistryValidation`, which asserted the *old* pre-fix behavior — a named `ai c 1` launch blocking on registry validation — and would have hard-crashed the process via a real unmocked launch attempt now that named launches skip discovery) and added a complementary targeted-launch test. 9 new/updated regression tests; full suite 1833 passed, 2 skipped; ruff clean on all touched files. Related: `[AI-CLI-79]` (prior auto-restart watcher bug, same `session_script.py` subsystem).

title: ai c N sessions not auto-reconnecting Remote Control; /rc command itself currently non-functional
description:
Sergei reports (2026-08-15, sw-6): new CC sessions still are not Remote-Control-connected from his phone, and separately /rc (/remote-control) is currently not working at all when tapped manually mid-session.

Related, already-closed issue: AI-CLI-165 (external_ref AI-CLI-165, closed 2026-08-02) root-caused the auto-reconnect gap as a stale .claude/.ai-cli-growthbook-toggle marker gate on session_script.py's pre-launch DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK override write, fixed by removing the marker predicate (commit 3254431, following an earlier unexplained revert bc056a8 of commit 1167672 that had first made the write unconditional).

Verified this session (2026-08-15): the fix is still intact in src/ai_cli/session_script.py (~line 448-464) -- the DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK pre-launch write is unconditional for engine==c, no marker check, matching the AI-CLI-165 fix. So this is NOT an obvious code reversion of that specific fix. Two live symptoms to chase instead:

1. Auto-reconnect still not happening on fresh 'ai c N' launches per Sergei's live report (separate from this session's own settings.local.json being absent, which is explained by sw-6 being a long-running --continue process across multiple /compact cycles -- the pre-launch write only fires at fresh process launch, so that absence alone is not evidence of a bug for THIS session; the bug is about genuinely fresh launches).
2. /rc / /remote-control itself failing when manually invoked (reported live, 2026-08-15) -- this is a different layer than the pre-launch toggle; could be a Claude Code CLI-side behavior change unrelated to our launcher.

Needs investigation to determine: (a) whether the pre-launch write is actually landing before 'claude' starts on a genuinely fresh ai c N launch (add logging/reproduce live), (b) whether the SessionStart-hook automatic-restore mechanism (rc-pair skill Step 4, aih-352 D-4/D-5) is registering correctly, (c) whether a recent Claude Code CLI release changed Remote Control / GrowthBook / /rc command behavior in a way that breaks this mechanism (separately being researched via a companion research task), or (d) something else. Root-cause via /bug-fix discipline (reproduce, root-cause, regression test if applicable, fix, verify, document) -- do not guess a patch without reproducing first.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified and documented for BOTH symptoms (auto-reconnect on fresh launch, and /rc failing manually). If an ai-cli-utils code fix applies, it is made, independently re-verified via live UAT (not just a sandboxed self-report), and a regression test added where testable. If the root cause is a Claude Code CLI product-side change outside this repo's control, that is documented explicitly (what changed, what release) and the bug is closed with a clear statement of what (if anything) our launcher needs to change to compensate, or that no compensating action is possible/needed.
notes:
2026-08-15/16, sw-6 second delegation pass: Codex implement traced the stable-session-template
deployment path and RC pairing/bridge registry state (no fixable ai-cli-utils code defect found;
manual /rc failure remains explained by the inherited DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK gate, unchanged from the
first pass). Shipped via ai-cli-utils PR #29.

2026-08-16, sw-6, post-reboot live UAT (mba-m3-24-sw): reframed the asymmetry as cross-repo, not
cross-session -- aih-1 (ai-harness) auto-reconnected RC at startup with zero taps; sw-1/sw-2/
sw-4/sw-6 (all sergei) all needed a manual /rc tap. Live diagnostics ruled out the simplest
explanations (bridge registry, env vars, settings.local.json, growthbook-toggle marker -- none
differed meaningfully) before delegating a third Codex pass with two candidate leads
(CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS 0-vs-1 by repo, and a template build-version skew).

THIRD DELEGATION PASS -- ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, SHIPPED AND MERGED: ai-cli-utils PR #31
(squash commit c5b33d04, merged 2026-08-16). Actual cause: an auto-update launch race in
_auto_update_if_stale() (src/ai_cli/main.py) -- it wrote the source-commit stamp BEFORE
confirming the child update subprocess succeeded, so a long-lived ai parent process kept
generating session templates from its already-imported (stale) module even though the stamp
claimed current. A freshly-invoked ai process (no stale import) got the correct template --
exactly matching the observed asymmetry (aih-1's deployed template was a same-day rebuild;
sw-*'s was not). CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS was investigated and found unsupported
(no discovered linkage to Remote Control eligibility in the installed client).

Fix: stamp is now written only after a successful update; the session-launch command re-execs
(via os.execvp) through the updated entry point before generating any template. Verified
independently (not just Codex's self-report): full suite re-run clean both before and after
resolving a merge conflict against a concurrent sw-4 PR (#30, same doc file) -- 2335 passed, 2
skipped both times; ruff/markdownlint/aido validate-doc all clean. CI on the PR showed the same
pre-existing, unrelated failures (test_quota.py Popen assertion; Windows-matrix git/tmux/ssh
tests) already failing on main at the same base SHA -- merged via admin bypass after confirming
that, not blind.

STILL OPEN pending live UAT (cannot be self-verified): once this fix is installed and a fresh
session launched for a previously-affected repo, confirm (a) its generated template contains the
DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK override and (b) Remote Control actually auto-reconnects at startup with zero
manual taps. If it still fails while a comparison session succeeds, that indicates a second,
different cause -- report upstream with exact Claude Code version + diagnostics, since the
launcher-side stale-generator path identified here would no longer explain it.
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed: auto-update launch race in _auto_update_if_stale (src/ai_cli/main.py), shipped via PR #31 (squash c5b33d04) with regression-test coverage, independently re-verified (full suite 2335 passed both before and after a merge-conflict resolution). Manual /rc failure (the original inherited-DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK explanation) also resolved this session. Live end-to-end UAT of zero-touch auto-reconnect on an affected Mac session is tracked separately as its own closable outcome: AI-CLI-70on.

title: ai c 6 resumed the wrong CC transcript (sw-6-2 instead of sw-6) sharing the same worktree cwd
description:
Reproduced live 2026-08-15: Sergei ran 'ai c 6' expecting to resume the 'sw-6' CC session (transcript e708efd4-bdb7-4a55-a1c8-997e9747adc8, correctly customTitle=='sw-6' throughout, 17MB/200 history entries, its prior process was an idle bg-spare killed earlier this session as a one-off workaround -- see AI-CLI-idle-claude-bg-wwaj). Instead it resumed a DIFFERENT session, transcript e2184270-60ed-44f2-b198-3b16abfa6dc3, customTitle=='sw-6-2' (a distinct named ai-cli slot the user created previously), 79MB/539 history entries, sharing the exact same cwd (~/projects/sergei/.worktrees/sw-6) because ai-cli-utils' worktree-per-slot model does not enforce one CC project directory per ai-cli session name -- both 'sw-6' and 'sw-6-2' share Claude Code's own project-directory key (~/.claude/projects/-Users-...-worktrees-sw-6/), which holds both transcripts side by side.

Orchestrating-session investigation so far (read src/ai_cli/session_script.py and src/ai_cli/main.py in full before assuming this is complete):
1. session_script.py has 4 distinct launch branches for engine=='c': (a) prompt_file exists -> bare 'claude --continue "" --name ...' with ZERO title resolution or touch; (b) no prompt_file -> calls 'ai internal resolve-continue-target "/Users/sergeiwallace/projects/sergei/.worktrees/sw-4" ""' (main.py's _find_cc_session_by_title, exact customTitle match, NOT substring -- verified both sessions' titles are correctly distinct, so naive title-collision is NOT the cause) and on a match, touches that file before '--continue' (relying on Claude Code's own --continue semantics of 'resume the most-recently-modified transcript in this project directory' -- the touch is a race-based workaround, not a direct --resume-by-id); (c) resolve_status==2 (a LIVE process already owns the matched transcript, per _cc_session_is_live's psutil-style PID+start-time verification) -> falls back to a FRESH '--continue'-less launch; (d) resolver found nothing AND resolve_status!=2 but the project directory has ANY jsonl file -> BARE 'claude --continue --name ...' with NO title matching and NO touch at all -- this is the branch most likely exercised if resolve-continue-target legitimately returned empty for some reason not yet identified.
2. Claude Code's own 'bg-spare' pre-warmed-background-process feature (a claude-binary-internal mechanism entirely -- zero references to 'bg-spare' anywhere in ai-cli-utils' own source) is a SEPARATE, faster attach path this repo's code has no visibility into or control over. title: ai c 1 — stale orphan worktree directory blocks launch on Windows
ai c bare-mode Windows — TUI corruption and keyboard handling broken (random chars, Shift+Enter, Ctrl+C)
Remote named-session launch preview identity does not match the server-allocated tmux session name
description:
Surfaced by AI-CLI-208's Round 2 audit (N-1,
docs/audits/ai-cli-208-session-naming-casing-audit.md) while verifying DV-1.
CONFIRMED pre-existing, unrelated to casing: verified against
src/ai_cli/main.py at commit 2519721^ (before any AI-CLI-206/208 casing
work) -- the pre-transport remote-preview line already never allocated an
index for a named remote session; it used the raw requested name verbatim
with no index suffix.

BUG: for a NAMED remote launch (e.g. "ai c --remote Planning"), the local
client emits an iTerm2 profile/title, leases a color slot, and constructs a
cleanup command using a locally-guessed session identity (e.g.
"c-r-app-planning") BEFORE the remote host actually runs
build_session_name()/find_next_index() and allocates the real, index-suffixed
session name (e.g. "c-r-app-planning-1"). The local preview and the actual
remote-created tmux session name diverge whenever an index gets appended --
which is every named launch, since named launches always go through
find_next_index(). Verified directly:
  preview: c-r-app-planning
  server:  c-r-app-planning-1
(AI-CLI-208's fix made both sides consistently lowercase, but did not, and
per its own casing-only scope should not have needed to, fix this
pre-existing index mismatch.)

IMPACT: the local machine's color-slot lease, iTerm2 profile/title, and the
"ai internal cleanup-session-files" cleanup command all target a session
name that is not the one actually created on the remote host. Cleanup in
particular may silently no-op against a name nothing ever uses.

ROOT CAUSE: the local machine cannot know the remote host's tmux occupancy
at preview-emission time (it runs before the SSH/mosh transport even
connects), so it cannot compute the same index the remote's
find_next_index() will independently allocate. A correct fix needs either
a remote preflight/handshake that returns the canonical allocated
session_id/ai_name before local profile/color/cleanup setup runs, or some
other mechanism to make named-session allocation deterministic across the
transport boundary -- this is a small protocol change, not a one-line fix.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- For a NAMED remote launch, the local client's iTerm2 profile/title
  emission, color-slot lease, and cleanup command all use the SAME session
  identity the remote host actually allocates via
  build_session_name()/find_next_index() -- not a locally-guessed,
  index-less preview.
- Numeric/bare remote launches (which don't require find_next_index() to
  break a tie -- the index is either explicit or trivially derivable) are
  unaffected if they already work correctly; verify they do as part of this
  fix.
- Regression test: named remote launch: local preview identity must equal
  the identity the remote-side build_session_name() call actually returns
  for the same inputs.

title: ai c <N> ignores an existing case/remote-differing worktree and session, creating a duplicate instead of resuming
description:
REPRODUCTION (Linux/Hetzner, case-sensitive filesystem -- confirmed live):
  1. A project's fleet-registry prefix is registered uppercase (e.g. "APP").
  2. An existing worktree + live tmux session were created earlier, before the
     prefix was uppercase, under the lowercase spelling: worktree
     .worktrees/app-7, tmux session named with a lowercase/no-remote-marker
     naming scheme (observed live case: the existing session is literally
     "c-r-app-7" -- lowercase prefix AND carrying the "-r-" remote-launch
     marker, meaning it was originally created via a remote (-R) launch when
     the prefix still resolved lowercase).
  3. Run "ai c 7" locally on that same machine (no -R flag). build_session_name()
     (session.py:498) computes ai_name purely from the CURRENT project_prefix
     verbatim plus the bare index -> "APP-7" uppercase, and computes the tmux
     session name the same way, with is_remote=False (no "-r-" segment) since
     this specific invocation is local -- neither matches the existing
     "c-r-app-7" session's actual name.
  4. find_next_index() (session.py:264) checks tmux occupancy via a
     "tmux has-session -t <computed-name>" call -- a case-sensitive,
     exact-string match against the computed "c-APP-7", which does not match
     the existing "c-r-app-7" session at all (differs in casing AND the
     remote-marker segment). It reports index 7 / slot "APP-7" as free.
  5. create_worktree("APP-7") (session.py:793, post AI-CLI-203/204/205 fixes)
     correctly does NOT collide with or delete the existing app-7 worktree
     (that class of bug is already fixed) -- but it DOES create a brand new,
     separate "APP-7" worktree and a brand new tmux session, entirely
     unrelated to the user's actual existing work.

IMPACT: the user runs "ai c 7" expecting to resume their existing session/
worktree, and instead gets a second, unrelated, freshly-created worktree +
session under a different name. This is confusing and, if the user starts
working in the new "APP-7" and forgets about "app-7", risks orphaning work in
whichever slot they don't return to. Not the same class of bug as AI-CLI-203
(which was about safety once a collision is detected) -- this is about
occupancy detection and slot resolution never recognizing the two as "the
same slot" in the first place.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis, needs verification during root-cause-and-fix): neither
find_next_index()'s tmux occupancy check nor build_session_name()'s naming
construction normalize for casing or for the is_remote ("-r-") segment when
deciding whether a given bare index is already in use. The fleet-registry
prefix casing can legitimately differ from how pre-existing sessions were
named (as observed live), and a session can legitimately have been created
either locally or remotely at different points in its life -- occupancy
detection needs to account for both when deciding "is slot N already taken",
even though the CURRENT invocation's own computed name may still need to
follow the current prefix casing and remote-flag for creating something new.

Distinct from, and not fixed by, AI-CLI-203/204/205 (create_worktree's
collision-safety and accurate create/reuse announcement) -- this is one layer
up, in how the session/worktree name and "already exists" determination are
computed BEFORE create_worktree is ever called.
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause verified with a minimal reproduction (unit or integration test)
  before the fix lands -- confirm exactly which mismatch(es) (casing,
  is_remote marker, or both) cause find_next_index/build_session_name to miss
  an existing worktree/session.
- "ai c <N>" (and "ai g <N>"), given a bare numeric index, finds and resumes/
  reuses an existing worktree + live session for that index even when it was
  created under a different prefix casing and/or a different is_remote state
  -- it must not silently create a second, parallel worktree+session for a
  slot that is already in use by the user's existing work.
- If genuinely ambiguous (e.g. two DIFFERENT existing sessions plausibly match
  index N under different casings), fail loudly with a clear diagnostic
  listing the candidates, rather than silently picking one or creating a new
  one.
- No change to create_worktree()'s collision-safety behavior from
  AI-CLI-203/204/205 -- this issue is about occupancy/name resolution
  upstream of that function, not the safety logic itself.
- Regression test reproduces the exact live scenario: an existing lowercase,
  remote-marker-carrying session/worktree; a later local "ai c <N>" invocation
  under a since-changed uppercase prefix; asserts it resumes the existing one
  rather than creating "PREFIX-N" fresh.
close_reason: Fixed and independently verified at commit 2519721: bare-index resolution now case-fold matches both local and remote tmux session name variants, and both local and case-alias worktree directories, before allocating a new slot. Full suite green (2300 passed), ruff clean. Regression tests added in test_session.py, test_bare_worktree.py, test_main.py, test_worktree_container_collision.py.

title: Worktree reuse after a failed creator initialization returns a not-fully-set-up worktree
description:
Round 3 Codex audit finding N-5 (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md),
found while verifying AI-CLI-203's concurrency hardening (commit 20a8436).

create_worktree()'s per-slot portalocker.Lock now spans registration probe
through git worktree add through post-creation initialization (upstream
setup, .venv/.claude/.gemini/.direnv symlinks, workspace trust, envrc
allowlisting) on the SUCCESS path. But if any of that post-add initialization
raises (upstream setup, symlink creation, trust registration, envrc
handling), the lock is still released (the portalocker.Lock context manager
exits on the exception) with no record that the worktree Git just registered
is only partially set up.

A second launcher waiting on the same slot then acquires the lock, re-probes
registration, finds the (now Git-registered but not-fully-initialized)
worktree, and returns it via the early registered-reuse path (session.py
around line 860) -- skipping ALL of the creator-only initialization block
entirely, since that block only runs on the "I just created it" path, not the
"I'm reusing an already-registered one" path.

IMPACT: a waiting session can launch into a worktree whose upstream tracking,
environment symlinks, workspace trust, or envrc approval was never
completed -- a degraded environment, not data loss, but a real correctness
gap in the concurrency contract this fix was meant to establish.

Verified by Codex via a mocked two-call probe: first call raised an upstream
init failure, second call returned a registered-but-not-created result --
i.e. reuse succeeded despite the creator having failed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Required initialization (upstream setup, symlinks, trust, envrc) is
  idempotent and is run/validated before BOTH the created-return and the
  reused-return paths, under the slot lock -- not skipped for reuse.
- On a creator's initialization failure, the worktree is preserved (not
  deleted -- consistent with the no-auto-delete policy), but the incomplete
  state is recorded or re-derivable so a later launcher retries
  initialization rather than returning an incompletely-set-up worktree as if
  it were ready.
- Regression test: a two-launch scenario where the creator raises during
  post-add initialization, and the waiter either (a) also fails loudly, or
  (b) completes the skipped initialization itself before returning -- it must
  never return a not-fully-initialized worktree as a bare success.
notes:
Fix attempt reverted 2026-08-10 (in-worktree, never shipped). Codex's first
attempt extracted a shared _initialize_worktree() helper and called it
unconditionally on BOTH the early registered-reuse path (top of
create_worktree, before any git worktree add) and the post-failed-add reuse
path -- not just the narrow N-5 recovery case.

This broke the common path hard: the early-reuse call hardcoded the branch
name as f"wt-{ai_name}" without verifying that is actually the branch the
registered worktree has checked out, so _set_upstream_or_raise() failed with
"branch does not exist" on ordinary worktree reuse/adoption -- 27 test
failures, mostly in test_session_adopt.py (real adoption scenarios, not
edge-case mocks). Independently verified in this session (not the audit
sandbox) with a full pytest run.

Reverted rather than iterated further -- the blast radius of a wrong fix here
(breaking everyday worktree reuse) is worse than leaving the narrow N-5 race
open. A safer design needs to: (1) determine the ACTUAL checked-out branch of
a registered worktree rather than assuming wt-<ai_name>, and (2) only mutate
upstream when it is verifiably missing/wrong (e.g. check current upstream via
git rev-parse first), not unconditionally on every reuse -- the symlink/trust/
envrc steps are naturally idempotent (they check existence first); the
upstream step is not, and needs the same treatment.

Left open, still P1 in principle, but not launch-blocking: this is a narrow
concurrent-launch-with-failed-initialization race, not a correctness issue in
the shipped, already-verified AI-CLI-203/204 fix. AI-CLI-203/204 remain closed
and shipped independent of this.
close_reason: Fixed at commit 4233a93 (third attempt) -- uses _current_branch() for real branch detection instead of assuming wt-<ai_name>, and a new _branch_upstream() check makes upstream-setting conditional instead of unconditional on reuse. Verified independently: full pytest (2294 passed), tests/test_session_adopt.py unmodified and passing (the exact file the prior attempt broke), ruff clean. New regression test uses real threads to force the creator-fails/waiter-completes race.

title: Case-insensitive filesystem collision in create_worktree can delete a live session's worktree
description:
On macOS (case-insensitive, case-preserving APFS), ai_name/worktree-dir casing is not
normalized anywhere in the launch path, and a case mismatch between the fleet-registered
project_prefix and an existing on-disk worktree directory produces a false "orphan
checkout" refusal -- or worse, an actual deletion of a live session's worktree.

REPRODUCTION:
  1. A project's project_prefix is registered as uppercase "APP" in the fleet registry
     (tier 1 / highest precedence in resolve_project_prefix(), config.py:645).
  2. An existing live session's worktree is `.worktrees/app-1` (lowercase) -- created
     under a different-cased prefix resolution previously in effect.
  3. Run `ai c 1` in that project again. build_session_name() (session.py:498) builds
     ai_name from project_prefix verbatim, no case normalization -> "APP-1".
  4. find_next_index() (session.py:264) checks tmux session names case-sensitively
     (`tmux has-session -t APP-1`) -- does not recognize `app-1`'s live tmux session
     as occupying the slot, hands back index 1 as "free".
  5. create_worktree() (session.py:793) builds wt_dir = .worktrees/APP-1.
     wt_dir.exists() is True because on a case-insensitive filesystem this is the
     SAME physical directory as .worktrees/app-1.
  6. registered_worktrees() (session.py:761) returns paths in the casing git
     recorded at creation time ("app-1"). The case-sensitive Python comparison
     `wt_dir.resolve() in registered_worktrees(repo_root)` fails even though
     wt_dir IS that exact registered worktree.
  7. _contains_git_checkout(wt_dir) (session.py:778) finds .git under the path
     (it's physically the live app-1 checkout) and create_worktree raises:
     "exists but is not a worktree of <repo>, and it contains a git checkout at
     <holder> -- refusing to delete it."

IMPACT: The refusal in step 7 is a lucky save, not the intended safety mechanism
firing correctly -- it happens to trip because a .git directory exists there. If
step 6/7's checkout-detection had NOT tripped (e.g. a differently-shaped collision),
the code path directly below runs `shutil.rmtree(wt_dir)` on the SAME PHYSICAL
DIRECTORY as the live, currently-running app-1 session's worktree -- silently
deleting a running session's checkout and any uncommitted work in it.

ROOT CAUSE: No component in the resolve_project_prefix -> build_session_name ->
create_worktree chain normalizes casing consistently, and none of the worktree/
tmux occupancy checks (find_next_index, registered_worktrees comparison,
wt_dir.exists()) are case-insensitive-filesystem-aware. A fleet registry's
uppercase prefix (chosen for a display-id convention, e.g. APP-a1b2) leaks
unchanged into filesystem/tmux-facing names, which historically were lowercase.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTIONS (for the implementer to evaluate, not prescriptive):
  1. Normalize project_prefix casing once at the point it's used for
     filesystem/tmux-facing names (ai_name, worktree dir, tmux session name),
     keeping the registry's original casing only for display-id use --
     these are two different consumers of the same string and don't need to
     share casing.
  2. Make find_next_index's tmux-session-name matching and create_worktree's
     wt_dir.exists()/registered_worktrees() comparison robust to case-insensitive
     filesystems (e.g. os.path.normcase-based comparison, or query git worktree
     list case-insensitively when the filesystem is case-insensitive).
  3. Regardless of 1/2, create_worktree's rmtree path should never fire based on
     a case-sensitive-only "not registered" determination on a case-insensitive
     filesystem -- add a same-file/same-inode check before treating an existing
     path as safe to delete.

A regression test should assert that a worktree dir colliding case-insensitively
with an existing registered worktree is never passed to shutil.rmtree.

RESOLVED 2026-08-10 at commit 23e8796: create_worktree() now compares candidates
against registered worktrees via Path.samefile filesystem identity, and the
shutil.rmtree recycle path was removed entirely in favor of an unconditional
refusal. A follow-up Codex audit (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md)
found 2 P1 residual issues (concurrent-creation misreporting, silent degradation
on identity/add errors) and several P2s tracked for a follow-up commit.
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause reproduced with a minimal test (or documented why not reproducible
  in CI, e.g. case-insensitive-fs-only) before the fix lands.
- create_worktree() never calls shutil.rmtree on a path that is case-insensitively
  the same file as an existing registered worktree.
- A new session launch with a case-differing prefix against an existing worktree
  either reuses the existing worktree correctly or fails loudly with an accurate
  diagnostic -- never silently deletes or silently duplicates.
- Regression test covers the exact repro: fleet-registry prefix casing differs
  from an already-materialized worktree directory's casing.

USER DIRECTIVE (2026-08-10) -- narrow the auto-delete path, don't just patch the
case bug around it:
- The existing "not a registered worktree -> shutil.rmtree" recycle path
  (session.py ~830-833) must never delete when there is ANY possibility of
  losing work: uncommitted changes, commits not pushed to any remote, or
  commits not merged/present on the integration branch (main/origin main) --
  regardless of whether a .git directory is detected there.
- Default preference is to NOT auto-delete at all: refuse and print the
  remediation command (matching the existing _contains_git_checkout refusal
  style), the same way the case-collision already (accidentally) does today.
  Auto-delete may remain ONLY for a directory that is provably empty of value
  (e.g. truly empty directory, or debris with no commits unreachable from any
  remote/local ref) -- implementer should treat "refuse by default, delete only
  when provably safe" as the required default, not a nuanced heuristic that
  still risks false positives.
- Add a regression test asserting create_worktree() refuses (does not rmtree)
  when the colliding directory has uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, or
  commits absent from the integration branch.

STATUS 2026-08-10: satisfied at commit 23e8796 (see RESOLVED note in description).
Residual audit findings tracked separately, not blocking this AC set.

Round 3 is the first pass to verify 20a8436, and found N-5 (worktree reuse after failed initialization, P1). title: Docs and memory assert ~/.local/share/uv is a cache, but it is the tool install dir — acting on it uninstalls the ai CLI
description:
A grep for the UV_CACHE_DIR environment variable name returns NOTHING on this machine, which reads as "the cache was never relocated". That is a FALSE NEGATIVE and acting on it is destructive.

The cache WAS relocated on 2026-07-28, by config file rather than env var. /home/sagemaker-user/.config/uv/uv.toml sets:

  cache-dir = "/home/sagemaker-user/user-default-efs/caches/uv"

Running "uv cache dir" confirms it resolves there, and that cache is a separate 3.1G living on EFS. That config file's own comment states why a config file was chosen over the env var: non-interactive and login shells do not source ~/.bashrc, so UV_CACHE_DIR alone left agent shells and hook subprocesses still writing into $HOME.

CONSEQUENCE. ~/.local/share/uv (1022M) therefore contains ZERO cache. It is:
  tools/  800M  -- aido 570M, ai-core 149M, ai-cli-utils 39M, copier 29M, pre-commit 15M
  python/ 223M  -- CPython 3.14.6 + 3.13.14, executed on every "uv run"

The 0-byte entries at ~/.local/bin/ai, aido, core, copier and pre-commit all point into tools/. So deleting ~/.local/share/uv, or relocating it to EFS, UNINSTALLS the ai CLI and every sibling tool. A disk-reclamation task nearly did exactly that on the strength of the false-negative grep.

This is the probe-adequacy failure mode in miniature: the grep RAN and returned cleanly, but it could not have come out the other way, because it looked in the wrong place. The check that actually distinguishes the two states is "uv cache dir", not a grep for the env var name.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Every doc, memory file, or bead comment asserting that ~/.local/share/uv is a cache, is disposable, or that the uv cache relocation is still pending is corrected. Search at minimum ai-cli-utils docs/ plus MEMORY.md, ai-harness docs/ plus the machine profiles, and any disk or cleanup bead.

AC-2 The canonical way to locate the uv cache is recorded as "uv cache dir" (authoritative: it honors the config file, the env var, and the platform default), with an explicit note that grepping for UV_CACHE_DIR is NOT sufficient, and why.

AC-3 ~/.local/share/uv is added to whatever do-not-delete list the fleet keeps for this machine, with the reason recorded (live tool installs; deleting it uninstalls the ai CLI).

AC-4 If any automated cleanup script or documented cleanup step targets ~/.local/share/uv, it is fixed or removed.

CONTEXT. Surfaced 2026-08-06 by the AI-CLI-173 disk analysis, which also found that the disk premise itself had expired: the home volume was resized from 5G to 100G and now reports 6% used with 95G free. Full write-up in sw-bms-workspace at docs/analysis/sagemaker-space-disk-pressure.md, commit b859be8.
close_reason: Fixed in 27a549c (merge of e53e9bf). Adds docs/procedures/uv-disk-usage-troubleshooting.md recording the three-directory structure (cache on EFS via ~/.config/uv/uv.toml, tools, interpreters), `uv cache dir` as the only reliable locator, and why grepping UV_CACHE_DIR is a false negative -- non-interactive and login shells never source ~/.bashrc, which is exactly why the config-file form was chosen on 2026-07-28. AC-1 audit was largely a CLEAN NEGATIVE and that is the useful finding: the two existing mentions (main.py tools-dir fallback comment, uv-hardlink bug doc) were already accurate, and no script, Makefile or documented cleanup step targets ~/.local/share/uv. The gap was missing guidance, not wrong code. Verified myself rather than from the agent report: 2112 passed / 0 failed, 221 hygiene+guard tests pass on the new doc, and the diff adds ZERO machine-specific paths or private tool names (checked, since the finding originated on a private machine and this is a public package). Nothing under ~/.local/share/uv or ~/.config/uv was modified.

title: 14 display IDs are double-allocated across two machines, so the dual-ID precommit gate blocks every .beads commit
description:
Blocks every commit that stages .beads/issues.jsonl in this repo. Surfaced 2026-08-05 while fixing the store/JSONL drift (AI-CLI-u9x / AI-CLI-fcl).

POSITIVE CONTROL, so this is not a new regression: the committed file at HEAD (43a6dab) already violates the invariant once, on AI-CLI-160 (AI-CLI-fae and AI-CLI-w4p both claim it). Resolving the drift raised the export from 158 to 172 records, which exposed 14 more. Counts: HEAD 158 records / 1 collision; post-reconciliation 172 records / 15 collisions.

ROOT CAUSE. bd-new serializes allocation with an flock on .beads/.displayid.lock and computes max(N)+1 from existing external_ref values. Both halves are per-store, so while this machine's Dolt store was diverged from the tracked JSONL, each machine computed max(N)+1 over a DIFFERENT record set and handed out the same N. The lock did its job; the input to max() was wrong. Every collision is one store-only issue against one JSONL-only issue, which is exactly the signature of two independent allocators, not of a lock race.

The collisions, AI-CLI-143 through 156 plus 160:
  143  urv (store-only)  vs 6tq (in HEAD)
  144  udn (store-only)  vs 7id
  145  v0u (store-only)  vs u9x
  146  n20 (store-only)  vs xnn
  147  vs8 (store-only)  vs z90
  148  v1t (store-only)  vs imn
  149  aq0 (store-only)  vs mda
  150  i0k (store-only)  vs lk8
  151  oea (store-only)  vs 50l
  152  2ff (store-only)  vs bc3
  153  fcl (store-only)  vs 70q
  154  8v4 (store-only)  vs oa8
  155  1db (store-only)  vs d2p
  156  b01 (store-only)  vs k1u
  160  fae             vs w4p   (pre-existing at HEAD)

WHY THIS WAS NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS. The gate prints a ready-made repair, bd update <id> --external-ref=AI-N --add-label=id:AI-N. Do not run it as printed: it hand-assigns display IDs, which the fleet rule forbids, and it invents a NEW prefix (AI- instead of AI-CLI-), so it would introduce a second ID namespace in this repo rather than repair the first. Choosing which side of each pair keeps its number is also not mechanical, because several of these IDs are already cited in commit messages and docs, so renumbering the wrong side silently invalidates those references.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1 Every external_ref in .beads/issues.jsonl is unique, and ~/.claude/bin/bd-precommit-validate passes on the staged file.
AC-2 For each of the 15 pairs, the side that keeps the number is the one already referenced in a commit message, doc, or plan; the other is renumbered above the current max. Record the decision per pair.
AC-3 Renumbering goes through the sanctioned path and keeps the AI-CLI- prefix; no hand-assigned IDs, no second prefix namespace.
AC-4 The id:PREFIX-N label and external_ref stay in agreement on every renumbered issue (bdx resolves both).
AC-5 A regression check that would have caught this: assert uniqueness of external_ref across the store AND the tracked JSONL, not just within whichever one is being written.
AC-6 The allocator no longer computes max(N)+1 from a single possibly-diverged source. Either reconcile before allocating or derive the ceiling from the union of store and tracked JSONL.

RELATED. Same defect class as ai-harness AIH-tpdl (22 duplicate display IDs in that store) and AIH-owd8 (the display-ID lock racing under concurrent sessions). AC-6 is the shared fix; the fleet-wide sweep belongs with those.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed in cda2d76. Adjudicated all 15 pairs from commit evidence rather than preference: 11 IDs stayed with the side already cited in a commit message or doc, and the 4 uncited pairs kept the older record. The other side of each pair was renumbered 162-176 under the .displayid.lock flock, keeping the AI-CLI- prefix. Did NOT use the repair the gate prints, which hand-assigns under a different prefix (AI-N) and would have opened a second ID namespace. Verified on origin/main by content: 173 records, 0 duplicate external_refs, 0 external_ref/label disagreements, no non-id labels destroyed. bd dual-ID precommit gate now PASSES. Root cause (bd-new computes max(N)+1 per store, so a diverged store yields a duplicate N) is the shared fix with AIH-tpdl/AIH-owd8 and stays open there.

title: test_given_stale_quota_cache_when_run_then_ai_statusline_part_called fails deterministically on main
description:
tests/test_quota.py::TestStatuslineScript::test_given_stale_quota_cache_when_run_then_ai_statusline_part_called FAILS on main:
  AssertionError: ai quota statusline-part should be called as a background refresh when cache is stale (>30s)
  assert False  where False = PosixPath('/tmp/.../ai_statusline_called').exists()

Reproduced in isolation (single test, -p no:randomly): 1 failed. So it is deterministic here, not an ordering artifact — though it may still be environment-sensitive (the test relies on a backgrounded refresh completing within a 1.5s sleep, which is timing-dependent by construction).

NOT caused by the uv --link-mode work (AI-CLI-148): the test's only external surfaces are PATH, a fake 'ai' shell shim, TMPDIR and the sentinel file — it never touches uv or the install path. Verified by reading the test body.

Contributes to the pre-push gate being red (4 failures on main: this one, the hygiene leak, and two uv-argv assertions already fixed).

INVESTIGATE: whether the stale-while-revalidate background refresh actually fires on this platform (the statusline script may spawn it in a way that does not survive, or the 1.5s window is too short under load), and whether the test should poll with a timeout instead of a fixed sleep. A fixed sleep in a concurrency assertion is the same wall-clock-dependence class as AI-CLI-158.
close_reason: Fixed in 4268f62: root cause was NOT a sleep race or lock file (both hypotheses refuted by a pristine-TMPDIR probe) — the test inherited an ambient CC_BILLING_MODE=api, which routes the statusline script down the cache-hit branch so the quota code never ran and the sentinel was never touched. Billing mode is now pinned in the test environment. Same ambient-process-state class as the GIT_DIR leak (AIH-353).

title: CC task namespace: writes land in an unrelated session-<hash> dir and completed tasks vanish, so namespace recovery cannot work
description:
MEASURED (2026-08-05, ai-cli-1 session, this machine):
- This session created 2 CC tasks and updated them 6 times. A content grep for their subjects across ALL of ~/.claude/tasks returned NOTHING.
- ~/.claude/tasks/session-f5b6cafa/ (matching this session's transcript UUID f5b6cafa-bc9e-455e-a6f3-89ab8ea02f98) EXISTS but holds 0 files.
- The only namespace written in the last 40 min is ~/.claude/tasks/session-c00b86c4/ — and its 4 tasks are kg-1's (KG-156..KG-159), not this session's.
- 814 namespace dirs exist; 795 (97.7%) hold zero json files.
- CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID is UNSET in this session (it is only exported by 'ai c <n>' launches, ai-cli-utils commit 9ada6d0), so this session is transcript-keyed.

TWO DISTINCT SYMPTOMS, both need root-causing (do not assume one cause):
(a) Completed tasks appear to be pruned from disk. The /task-panel recovery procedure greps for status pending/in_progress, so a cleanly-completed session leaves an EMPTY namespace and recovery finds nothing. If pruning is intended, the recovery procedure's premise is wrong and must be rewritten; if not, it is data loss.
(b) A namespace's name does not reliably correspond to the session that writes it. session-f5b6cafa exists-but-empty while an unrelated session-c00b86c4 receives writes. Determine what actually derives the key (CC internal, not documented in our skill) before proposing any fix.

CONSEQUENCE: the /task-panel skill's orphan-recovery path (~/.claude/skills/task-panel, steps 3a-3f) cannot recover this session's tasks after a crash — verified live today. It also risks adopting ANOTHER session's tasks: the only recoverable candidates on this machine carry kg-* and SageMaker-infra subjects.

IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this is CC-harness behavior, not necessarily an ai-cli-utils defect. The fix may be (1) always pin CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID rather than only via 'ai c', (2) correct the /task-panel skill's documented premise, (3) an upstream CC report, or some combination. Root-cause FIRST; do not implement before the mechanism is established. Verify claims against CC's actual behavior rather than our skill's description of it — the skill has already been shown wrong here.

Blocks the CC-task-migration step of AI-CLI-149 (session-adopt): moving task files is meaningless until it is known where CC actually reads them from.
close_reason: Root-caused: TWO independent Claude Code harness defects (2.1.222), neither an ai-cli-utils bug. (1) A 5s-debounced sweeper deletes every task file in a namespace once ALL its tasks are 'completed', writing the highest id to .highwatermark first. Proven by that ledger: independently re-verified 10/10 .highwatermark files exist iff the id sequence has a gap, each value == highest missing id; negative control = ZERO of 814 namespaces retain an all-completed set; 15 completed tasks DO survive, all in namespaces that also hold an open task. So completion alone does not delete — the all-completed condition does. (2) The namespace key is the active TEAM name (per-process, regenerated every start incl. --continue), not the transcript UUID — one transcript spread tasks over 4 namespaces. This session's own session-f5b6cafa has hw=4 with zero files, explaining the original report exactly. CONSEQUENCE: /task-panel orphan recovery is structurally broken (its live-exclusion step names 2 non-live namespaces, excludes neither live one, and selects a LIVE session's dir). NO code fix needed here: ai-cli-utils already pins CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID, the highest-precedence resolver branch and a complete mitigation; the reporting session simply was not launched via 'ai c'. Doc: docs/bugs/cc-task-namespace-persistence.md (BUG-011). Commit 4268f62. NOT established: whether the wipe is intentional (undocumented is proven, 'bug' is not); the no-teams fallback path; single host/version only.

title: ai session-adopt: adopt a non-ai-c CC session into a worktree — transcript, tasks, memory, and worktree creation in one validated command
description:
Extends the shipped 'ai cc-migrate' (AI-CLI-144, transcript-only) into a full session-adoption command so any CC session started WITHOUT 'ai c' can be resumed by 'ai c <n>' from the right repo, losing nothing.

MEASURED CURRENT STATE (2026-08-05, this machine):
- 187 transcripts total, only 11 titled. Titled sessions and their cwd:
    kg-1     64.67 MB / 20068 lines  -> kg repo ROOT (needs worktree .worktrees/kg-1)   [LIVE, do last]
    aih-1    14.23 MB /  7683 lines  -> ai-harness ROOT (needs worktree)
    aido-1    7.79 MB /  4695 lines  -> already in .worktrees/aido-1 (OK)
    kg-2       7.28 MB / 3017 lines  -> already in .worktrees/kg-2 (OK)
    kg-3       5.90 MB / 2708 lines  -> already in .worktrees/kg-3 (OK)
    ai-cli-1   4.78 MB / 2440 lines  -> ai-cli-utils ROOT (needs worktree)             [LIVE, do last]
    aih-2      2.86 MB / 1297 lines  -> ai-harness ROOT (needs worktree)
    acto-1     1.57 MB /  837 lines  -> acto ROOT (needs worktree)
    kg-3       0.83 MB /  419 lines  -> kg repo ROOT (DUPLICATE title vs the worktree kg-3 — the fail-loudly case)
    aih-3      0.79 MB /  398 lines  -> already in .worktrees/aih-3 (OK)
    proj-1     0.53 MB /  232 lines  -> ~/projects (not a repo; surface for a decision)
- Untitled transcripts >1MB: ZERO. All 176 untitled are <1MB and are pytest sandboxes / /tmp probes — per Sergei, not worth migrating.
- Only kg-1 (pid 2855875) and ai-cli-1 (pid 2923882) are live processes.

SCOPE — one command, must handle:
1. Worktree: create the target worktree if absent (off fresh origin/main, per the repo's own convention); if it already exists, USE it. Never clobber.
2. Duplicate-title collision (the real 'kg-3' case above): a transcript at the repo root sharing a customTitle with one already in the target worktree must FAIL LOUDLY and present options (retitle + adopt to a new index, keep-both, skip), never silently pick one. 'ai c' resolves by first customTitle, so a duplicate makes resume nondeterministic.
3. Transcript: reuse cc_migrate.migrate_session (already verifies line count before deleting the source; preserves mtime).
4. CC tasks: move/merge ~/.claude/tasks/<old-ns>/*.json into the pinned namespace (~/.claude/tasks/<ai_name>/). IDs are namespace-scoped, so a merge must not clobber an existing N.json — renumber and report. NOTE: depends on the namespace-persistence defect filed separately.
5. Memory: ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ — cc_migrate deliberately skips this because other sessions may share the source root. Adoption must handle it explicitly (copy vs move vs merge) with a stated rule, not silence.
6. Anything else keyed by the project slug rather than the session UUID — inventory it first and state what is intentionally left alone (UUID-keyed state is unaffected by design).

REQUIREMENTS: dry-run default or a mandatory --dry-run/-n preview; per-session validation with a probe that can fail (post-adopt, assert 'ai c <n>' actually resolves that transcript); idempotent (re-running adopts nothing); refuses to touch a LIVE session (check /proc for the pid in ~/.claude/sessions/*.json) — kg-1 and ai-cli-1 must be rejected while running; bulk mode over all titled sessions with a per-session skip/continue; both short and long option forms (repo CLI convention).

PRECONDITION: /home/sagemaker-user is at 87% of 5.0G (660M free) and kg-1's transcript alone is 64MB. A copy-then-verify adoption doubles a transcript transiently, so the command must check free space before writing and fail cleanly rather than ENOSPC mid-write (an ENOSPC here corrupts the transcript being migrated).

DOC: a procedure doc covering the whole flow so this is repeatable by hand if the command is unavailable.
notes:
DECISION 2026-08-05 (Sergei) — duplicate-title collision handling is RETITLE-TO-FREE-INDEX, and it is ALWAYS a hard human gate.

Required behavior for the collision case (the real kg-3 instance: a 0.83 MB transcript titled 'kg-3' at the kg repo root vs the 5.90 MB one already in .worktrees/kg-3):
1. DETECT the collision before touching anything and STOP. Never auto-resolve, never pick by size/mtime, never silently skip. Exit non-zero with the two candidates printed (title, size, line count, cwd, mtime) so the human can tell them apart.
2. OFFER retitle-to-free-index as the primary remedy: compute the lowest unused index for that repo's prefix (scan existing customTitles + existing worktrees so the chosen index collides with neither), and show the exact proposed new title.
3. REQUIRE explicit human confirmation of the new index before writing. A --yes/-y style blanket confirm must NOT cover this case: the gate is unconditional even in --all/bulk mode, which should pause on the collision, report it, and continue with the remaining sessions rather than aborting the batch.
4. Retitle means rewriting the customTitle records in the transcript (the resume path matches on the FIRST titled record — see cc_migrate.transcript_title) and adopting into the worktree for the NEW index. Verify post-adopt that 'ai c <new-index>' resolves the retitled transcript and 'ai c <old-index>' still resolves the original.

Suggested surface: -c/--on-collision {gate,retitle} defaulting to 'gate', plus -T/--new-title TITLE and -I/--new-index N to supply the human's answer non-interactively on a second invocation. Keep both short and long forms per repo convention. Do NOT add a 'force'/'auto' collision mode — the gate is the requirement, not a default.
close_reason: SHIPPED 2026-08-06 as commit 93685ec: src/ai_cli/session_adopt.py (784 lines), tests/test_session_adopt.py (999 lines), docs/tools/cc-session-adoption.md. 2112 passed / 0 failed, 100% coverage on session_adopt.py, no pragma. Proven in real use: all four non-live adoptions (aih-1, aih-2, acto-1, kg-3-root to kg-4) completed via this command, and its unconditional title-collision gate correctly refused the kg-3 duplicate and proposed a free index. The one remaining open item — the live-session refusal being proven with os.getpid() rather than a real CC process — is split out as AI-CLI-181 so it keeps its own identity rather than holding this closed-outcome issue open.

title: ai c derives wrong prefix for worktrees, session titles and beads ids -- registry never populated
description:
`ai c` derives the wrong prefix for worktrees, session titles, and beads ids because the project registry is never populated on a new machine.

SYMPTOM: a worktree named `wt-ai-1` in ai-cli-utils. The correct prefix is the project's registered alias (AI-CLI, matching its beads prefix), not `ai`. Sergei reported it 2026-08-03 on bms-windows-sem-kg.

ROOT CAUSE, verified rather than assumed:
- ai-cli's config on this machine resolves to C:/Users/wallas12/AppData/Roaming/ai-cli-utils/config.toml (get_xdg_config_home(), NOT ~/.config/ai-cli -- worth knowing, since looking in the POSIX location shows nothing and reads as "no config at all").
- That file exists but is the UNTOUCHED DEFAULT TEMPLATE: `main_project` is still commented out under [project], and there is no project registry section with per-project prefixes.
- config.py load_config() writes DEFAULT_CONFIG on first use and never registers anything, so a fresh machine gets a config that parses fine and carries no project mappings. Nothing prompts, nothing fails.

WHY `wt-ai-1` SPECIFICALLY: `ai-cli-utils`[:3] == `ai`. That is the cwd-derived fallback AI-CLI-88 was closed for removing (`cwd.name[:3]`, the 'myproject'-style ghost session). Either the fallback survives on a path AI-CLI-88 did not cover, or a second copy of that logic exists for WORKTREE naming while AI-CLI-88 only fixed SESSION resolution. Determine which before fixing -- if it is the latter, the same latent bug affects every repo and AI-CLI-88 should not have been closed as fully fixed.

SCOPE OF THE FIX:
1. Establish correct prefixes for every repo root Sergei launches sessions from, at minimum: ai-harness (AIH), ai-cli-utils (AI-CLI), ai-core (CORE), aido (AIDO), bms-semantic-knowledge-graph (KG), sw-bms-workspace (KG -- note it HOSTS the KG store for the semantic-kg work, so decide deliberately whether these two share a prefix or need distinct ones; today both use KG).
2. Make the prefix ONE source of truth used by all three consumers -- git worktree names, CC session custom titles, and beads display-id prefixes. They currently disagree, which is why a `wt-ai-1` worktree can coexist with an AI-CLI beads store.
3. AUTO-CONFIGURE ON A NEW MACHINE. This is the durable half: a fresh machine must arrive with the registry populated, not with a default template. AI-CLI-62 (open, P1, "Proactive project registry registration") already proposes `ai register --project --prefix --type`, registry opt-in, and a self-describing `[tool.ai-cli]` block in pyproject.toml -- that is the right mechanism; this issue is the concrete driver for it. Wire it into machine provisioning (ai-harness install.sh / scripts/bootstrap) so it is not a manual step.
4. FAIL LOUDLY rather than guessing. Any unresolvable prefix should error with the remedy, never silently truncate a directory name -- the AI-CLI-88 principle, applied to worktree and title derivation too.

Related: AI-CLI-62 (the mechanism), AI-CLI-88 (closed, same class of bug, may be incompletely fixed), AI-CLI-103 (expand config.toml coverage). Cross-repo: ai-harness AIH-604 / AIH-606 cover provisioning and the folded-in bootstrap that should carry this registration.

Also pending: delete the stray `wt-ai-1` worktree once it is confirmed merged and pushed (hard human gate per ai-harness AIH-603 R8).

title: test_weekly_pace_shown_as_magnitude_color_encodes_direction is non-hermetic — calls real datetime.now() before its own time-mock, fails intermittently, blocks all pushes
description:
Found 2026-08-02 ~19:00 EDT while pushing an unrelated history-linearization fix to main.

tests/test_quota.py's _capture() helper (used by this test) calls
qdb._get_current_week_start() to establish week_start_str BEFORE entering the
with patch("datetime.datetime") block that mocks "now" for the rest of the test.
_get_current_week_start() falls back to datetime.now(timezone.utc) when no now
argument is passed (quota_db.py:191-198), so the anchor week boundary the test
computes its "fixed" 161-hours-elapsed offset from is itself derived from REAL
wall-clock time, not a fixed point.

test_weekly_pace_shown_as_magnitude_color_encodes_direction expects "17% usage,
161h elapsed (~96% of week) -> -79% delta" but got -76% at measurement time --
consistent with the real "current week" boundary shifting the effective elapsed
fraction depending on when the test actually runs, despite the test author's intent
that hours_elapsed=161 be a fully fixed synthetic scenario.

Impact: this makes the test flaky against real time rather than fully hermetic, and
since it runs in the repo's local pre-push test-gate hook, a failure here blocks
ALL pushes to ai-cli-utils main -- not just ones touching quota code -- until either
real time drifts back into the window the hardcoded expected values assume, or the
test is fixed.

Fix direction (not yet investigated in depth): either pass a fixed now into
_get_current_week_start() inside _capture() so the whole scenario is deterministic,
or change the test's assertions to compute their expected percentages from the same
_get_current_week_start()-derived boundary the code under test uses, rather than a
hardcoded "79%"/"~96%" comment-derived constant.
close_reason: Fixed: _capture() now passes a fixed reference instant into _get_current_week_start() instead of falling back to real datetime.now(). Commit cc77f79 (ai-cli-utils main). Full suite verified green (2009 passed) before push.

title: Auto-update stamp is written before the update runs, latching a failed host behind forever

comments.author: T
comments.text:
Found while root-causing AI-CLI-132 (stranded autostash); deliberately NOT fixed there because it needs its own design.

`_auto_update_if_stale` (src/ai_cli/main.py) writes its stamp file keyed on the CURRENT HEAD *before* running `ai update --force`. If the update cannot advance HEAD, the early-return then matches that same hash forever and auto-update never retries.

Measured live on the remote build host: stamp file and HEAD were both 4711d4e, and the host had not auto-updated for five days.

AI-CLI-132 removes the way HEAD gets frozen in the first place, so this is no longer reachable by that route — but the latch itself is still there for any other cause of a failed update.

NOT a one-line move of the write. Writing the stamp only on success means every subsequent `ai` invocation retries a failing update, which is presumably why it was written this way. Needs a real retry policy (backoff, attempt counter, or stamp-on-attempt plus a separate success marker).

title: Guard the harm, not the cause: block commits that delete files still live on origin/main
description:
AIH-443's genesis is still unknown after three investigations. This issue stops arguing with that and closes the damage path instead.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED:
- Shape A: git-tracked symlinks a sub-agent checkout never materialized.
- Shape B: 'git pull --rebase --autostash' exiting 0 after its stash pop conflicted.
- Shape C: pre-commit's staged_files_only.py writes unstaged changes to a patch, runs 'git checkout -- .' (which RESTORES the file), runs hooks, then re-applies the patch in its finally block (which RE-DELETES it). Located at pre_commit/staged_files_only.py L53-86.
- Genesis -- what deletes the file in the first place -- is NOT identified. An agent narrowed it to a one-second window (a pull --rebase --autostash at 20:22:16, the deletion patch at 20:22:17) but correctly refused to name a file:line it could not prove.

CRITICAL FRAMING, do not get this wrong: pre-commit is NOT the bug and must NOT be patched. Restoring unstaged changes after running hooks is its correct designed behavior, and a deleted file is a legitimate unstaged change -- someone who ran 'rm' intending to commit that deletion needs it preserved. It is also third-party. 'Fixing' it would break real workflows.

THE INSIGHT: you cannot reliably distinguish an intentional 'rm' from a phantom deletion -- that is structural, since 'rm' + 'git add -A' and 'git rm' produce identical index states. But you do not need to. The missing file is harmless and recoverable from HEAD. The HARM is committing that deletion to main. Guard the outcome, not the cause, and the fix holds regardless of how many genesis shapes exist.

Existing detection is a warning at launcher time (detect_phantom_deleted_files, branch worktree-aih443-shapec, commit 50886a5, unpushed). That is an alarm, not a guard -- a warning printed at launch does not stop a 'git commit -a' twenty minutes later.

Note this rule has been hand-written into roughly ten sub-agent briefs today ('do not commit any file deletion you did not intend'). A rule that must be retyped into every delegation is a rule that belongs in code.

WORTH RESEARCHING FIRST, and route it Codex -> Gemini -> CC per fleet policy: is there a known interaction between 'git pull --rebase --autostash' and pre-commit's post-merge hook that drops a tracked file? The one-second window above is a specific, checkable question with a possible published answer, and two root-cause guesses were already wrong today.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: A pre-commit-stage guard rejects any commit containing a deletion of a tracked file that is still present on origin/main, unless the deletion is explicitly acknowledged.
AC-2: The acknowledgement path is usable and documented -- intentional deletions must remain easy, or the guard gets bypassed and becomes worse than nothing.
AC-3: The guard is PROVEN able to fail: stage a real phantom deletion, watch it reject; stage an acknowledged deletion, watch it pass. Both directions demonstrated.
AC-4: pre-commit itself is NOT patched, wrapped, or worked around.
AC-5: Distributable beyond one repo -- the same class of loss applies fleet-wide.
AC-6: The research question above is answered or explicitly recorded as unanswerable, before genesis is declared un-findable.

title: Runaway loop re-ran _refresh_live_session_scripts ~9M times in 2 minutes, emitting 1.1 GB of output
description:
Found 2026-07-27 by forensics on a 1.1 GB junk file, before deleting it.

THE ARTIFACT: `sergei/.worktrees/sw-1/typescript` — 1,164,748,852 bytes, produced by the Unix
`script(1)` command (which writes to a file of exactly that name). Its own header and footer bound
the window precisely:

    Script started on Fri Jul 24 21:25:16 2026
    Script done   on Fri Jul 24 21:27:16 2026

**Two minutes. 1.1 GB.**

WHAT IS IN IT: sampling at the 500 MB and 700 MB offsets shows one line repeating, per live
session, interleaved with full-screen repaint escapes (`ESC[H` cursor-home, `ESC[K` erase-line):

    refreshed session template: c-aih-1
    refreshed session template: c-aih-2
    refreshed session template: c-kc-1
    refreshed session template: c-sw-1
    refreshed session template: c-sw-3
    refreshed session template: c-sw-6

That string exists in exactly one place: `src/ai_cli/main.py:373`, inside
`_refresh_live_session_scripts()`.

RATE: 8,160 occurrences per sampled MB x ~1,110 MB = roughly **9 million** emissions in 120
seconds, about **75,000 per second**.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT: `_refresh_live_session_scripts()` iterates live tmux sessions ONCE per
call and prints one line per managed session. It contains no loop of its own. So the function is
not the bug — **something called it, or its caller, several million times.** Its docstring says it
is "called after `ai update` installs a new template", which makes the auto-update / auto-restart
path the first place to look. Do not assume that is the answer; establish it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE DISK: 75k iterations/second means each one also ran
`tmux list-sessions` (a subprocess) and `_write_stable_session_script()` (a file write with a
chmod). For two minutes. That is a subprocess-and-write storm against the tmux server and the
state dir, not merely noisy logging. Nobody noticed at the time; it surfaced three days later only
because a stray `script` recording made it physically large.

The 1.1 GB file has been deleted (untracked debris, no unique content) after this evidence was
extracted. The forensic detail above is the record — it cannot be re-derived.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1 The loop that invoked this ~9M times is identified by file:line, with the trigger condition
     that made it spin. If it cannot be identified, say so explicitly and state what was ruled
     out — a guessed cause recorded as fact is worse than an open issue.
AC-2 The loop is bounded, or made incapable of re-entering at this rate.
AC-3 Proven by reproducing the trigger and showing the invocation count bounded — before the fix
     it must be shown unbounded. A run that simply completes proves nothing.
AC-4 `_refresh_live_session_scripts()` gains a guard so a pathological caller cannot turn it into
     a subprocess storm (rate limit, idempotence check, or a no-op when nothing changed).
AC-5 No `--no-verify` / `SKIP=` in the fix or its verification.

comments.text:
AC-1 ANSWER, recorded by the lead because the agent had no bd access from its worktree.

The '~9M invocations / 75k per second subprocess storm' premise in the original brief was WRONG, and I propagated it. It is arithmetically impossible and I verified that independently: this machine forks+execs 'tmux list-sessions' at 32/sec (agent measured 38). One refresh call = one tmux fork+exec + 6 printed lines, so 9M lines = 1.5M calls in 120s = 12500 calls/sec required. That is ~390x above what the hardware does. A probe that returns 32 when the theory needs 12500 is a decisive negative control.

What the 1.1 GB file actually was: 1.11 GB / 9M occurrences = 122 bytes each, against ~44 bytes for the bare line + CRLF. The remaining ~78 bytes/line are ESC[H / ESC[K full-screen repaint escapes. So it is a terminal repainting a screen whose scrollback held ONE 'ai update' output -- not 1.5M fresh invocations. If that reading holds, the repaint source is CC's own TUI renderer, outside this repo, and is NOT fixed here. AC-1 is therefore answered as: no caller loop exists; the emitter's only caller is _do_update_or_deploy() at main.py:985, which self-disarms via the last_update_commit.txt stamp written before spawning.

A DIFFERENT, real runaway loop was found and fixed in the same auto-restart path -- session_script.py:287 ran 'read -t 1 -r < /dev/null', which returns instantly on EOF rather than waiting out its timeout, so the watcher's 'while true' busy-spun for the life of every session. I verified this directly: 5 iterations of the buggy form took 0.084s where correct behaviour is 5.0s. Every counter-derived duration (30-tick heartbeat, 10-tick startup grace, 10-tick config check) was wrong by the same factor. Fixed to 'sleep 1'.

Shipped as 6cbaaef on origin/main. 1856 passed / 7 skipped, up from 1850 baseline. All three guards proven able to fail by mutation.

Lesson for the record: I asserted a mechanism in a delegation brief without checking whether the hardware could produce it. Same failure as the worktree-upstream-drift root cause earlier the same day. Check whether the mechanism is POSSIBLE before it becomes the brief an agent works from.

title: ccF Fable statusline meter is structurally dead — Anthropic removed the per-model quota surface it scraped
description:
Sergei, 2026-07-26: "ccF (fable) usage quota % is still at 2% even though i'm pretty sure we've
run a fable agent... it's usage quota % increases notably whenever we run it, from what ive
observed."

CONFIRMED A BUG, and confirmed independently by the driver rather than on the audit agent's word.

ROOT CAUSE: `ai_cli/quota.py::_scrape_usage_hidden_pane()` gets the Fable number by spawning a
hidden tmux session, launching an interactive `claude`, typing `/usage`, and regex-scraping a
"Current week (Fable)" progress-bar line. **That line no longer exists.** Reproduced by hand
twice against the currently-installed CC v2.1.220 (day view and week view): the dialog now shows a
"What's contributing to your limits usage?" section — session-characteristics text plus
Skills/Subagents-by-name attribution tables — which is not a quota bar and is not keyed by model
at all. The repo's own research doc (`docs/research/claude-quota-statusline-rate-limits-2026.md`,
written 2026-07-13 against CC 2.1.207) confirms the line existed then and was the SOLE per-model
source, so this is an upstream removal somewhere between 2026-07-25 evening and 2026-07-26.

DRIVER-VERIFIED from `~/.local/state/ai-cli/quota.db` directly:
- `weekly_sonnet_pct` last had a non-null value at **2026-07-25T23:07:23Z** (value 2.0), and had
  been 2.0 for **239 consecutive snapshots** before that.
- Every snapshot since is **NULL** for Fable while `usage_percent` (all-models) climbed 55% -> 57%
  in the same window. The two feeds are provably decoupled.
- `~/.local/state/ai-cli/fable-scrape-backoff.json` shows `misses: 4`, backoff already maxed at the
  120-min ceiling. The code's own instrumentation knew it was failing.

So the Fable coordinator plus five sub-agents run on 2026-07-26 COULD NOT have moved this meter
regardless of actual usage. This is not the transient server-side rate-limit the code's comments
assume.

THE OTHER TWO METERS ARE FINE (verified with positive controls, not absence-of-error):
- ccWk (Claude weekly): reads `rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage` from CC's own statusLine
  stdin JSON. Observed climbing in ~10-minute steps; a fresh live `/usage` capture matched.
- cxWk (Codex weekly): live JSON-RPC to `codex app-server --stdio` `account/rateLimits/read`,
  300s cache. A fresh independent call returned byte-identical to the cache.

NEAR-MISS ON SILENT FAILURE — worth its own attention. The display is not strictly lying: the
stale-past-2h marker does render (`ccF 2% ->73% (clock glyph)`, confirmed via `od -c`). But it is
one dim low-contrast character next to a normally-coloured "2%" and a green "->73%" pace delta —
and that delta is now meaningless, since it is `frozen_pct - elapsed_time_pct`, growing every day
purely because time passes while the numerator is frozen. At a glance it reads as a healthy meter.

THE DECISION THIS ISSUE NEEDS (not a patch — there is no replacement data source):
(a) Past some staleness threshold, replace the number with an explicit unavailable state
    (`ccF n/a (stale 5d)`) and suppress the pace arrow. Threshold suggested at 24-48h.
(b) Find a new proxy — e.g. the new Skills/Subagents attribution tables. Lossy, and not
    Fable-specific.
(c) Drop per-model tracking entirely until Anthropic exposes one again.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1 A stale meter renders as unmistakably unavailable, not as a plausible coloured percentage.
AC-2 The pace-delta is suppressed whenever its numerator is stale — a delta computed from a frozen
     value is worse than no delta.
AC-3 Whatever source is chosen, its disappearance fails LOUDLY rather than pinning the last value.
     The current design's failure mode is the bug, not the missing line.
AC-4 Proven by simulating source loss and showing the display state change — a check that cannot
     distinguish "fresh 2%" from "frozen 2%" proves nothing.
