title: DONE 2026-07-20: watcher now hashes `.claude/settings.json` (global + project) and `.mcp.json` alongside `CLAUDE.md`
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-115]` **DONE 2026-07-20: watcher now hashes `.claude/settings.json` (global + project) and `.mcp.json` alongside `CLAUDE.md`** (`session_script.py`'s `_config_watch_files`), with regression coverage in `tests/test_config_watch_hash.py` (6 tests: real-bash hash-change behavioral checks for each watched file + a stability sanity check, not just string presence). Full test suite (1843 tests) green. **Auto-restart config-change watcher never hashes `.claude/settings.json` — only `CLAUDE.md` — so `env` overrides (e.g. `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE`) silently never propagate to already-running sessions** — Filed 2026-07-20 (Sergei + Claude, root-caused live). `session_script.py`'s idle-triggered auto-restart (`config_reload_idle_secs`, default 90s) exists specifically so a config edit propagates to a long-running CC session without a manual kill — but its change-detection hash (`session_script.py` ~line 240) only covers `$HOME/projects/CLAUDE.md` + `$(pwd)/CLAUDE.md`. It never hashes `.claude/settings.json` (global `~/.claude/settings.json` or any project-level `<repo>/.claude/settings.json`), even though that file's `env` block is exactly the kind of process-launch-only config (like `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`) that needs a real process restart to take effect — `/compact` does not re-read it. **Concrete incident:** sergei commit `87eacfe6` (2026-07-18 21:57) removed `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=70` from `sergei/.claude/settings.json` to restore the native ~96.7% auto-compact threshold. sw-1 (pid 88380) had launched the prior evening (Jul 17 21:29) and ran continuously through the fix — the watcher never detected the settings.json change (it doesn't watch that file), so no idle-restart ever fired, and the override stayed baked into that process's env for 2+ days across ~6 compactions. On 2026-07-20 it fired auto-compact again at the stale 70%-of-window boundary, reproducing the exact "ctx-pct read ~66%" symptom the original fix commit's own message described — because ctx-pct reports the real full-window %, which doesn't land exactly on the override's own percentage base. **Fix:** extend the watcher's hash to also cover `.claude/settings.json` (global + project-level, same two-path pattern already used for CLAUDE.md) so `env`-block edits trigger the same idle-restart CLAUDE.md edits already get. Scope-design first (is `env` the only settings.json key that needs this, or should the whole file be hashed?) before implementing. Related: sergei commits `7315f0e2` (added the override), `87eacfe6` (removed it, documents the same 66%-vs-70% confusion), `ai-harness` `f38c1c4` (ctx-pct override-aware reporting — already correct, not the bug).

title: `ai c`/`ai g` launcher doesn't activate direnv before starting the agent — fleet-wide stale/missing-secrets exposure
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-112]` **`ai c`/`ai g` launcher doesn't activate direnv before starting the agent — fleet-wide stale/missing-secrets exposure** — Filed 2026-07-19 (Claude, sw-1), from `docs/research/cc-bash-tool-direnv-env-loading.md` (Codex research, `cx research --effort high`). Root cause: the launcher `chdir`s to the resolved project/worktree in Python or a generated non-login zsh script, then invokes `claude`/`gemini` directly — no `direnv exec`/export evaluation at any point. Combined with Claude Code's Bash tool never activating direnv itself (separate, already-documented finding — `sergei/docs/procedures/secrets-management.md` § Agentic CLI and non-interactive shell loading), this means an agent session's actual secrets/env state depends entirely on whatever the parent shell had at `ai c`/`ai g` launch time — stale if a session is long-running past a Doppler rotation, wrong-but-valid if launched with a lingering override, or silently missing if launched from a shell that never `cd`'d into a populated project. Demonstrated concretely via AIDO-252 (a stale `AIDO_DB_DSN` override silently won for an entire session). **Scope:** run the generated session process under `direnv exec <target_root> <agent-or-session-command>` once the launcher has resolved the final project/worktree root — apply to every launch/restart variant (normal, `--once`, bare, explicit `-p`, worktree and no-worktree, new tmux session, restart/hot-reload, resume/continue, remote SSH/mosh, both Claude and Gemini) — wrapping only the first invocation is insufficient if a later restart path re-invokes the binary outside the activated subtree. Acceptance criteria + required regression-test list are fully spelled out in the research doc's Recommendation §1 and "Required regression tests" — use those directly, don't re-derive. **Related:** the research doc above (full analysis + 3-layer recommendation, this is layer 1 of 3), `sergei/docs/procedures/secrets-management.md` (layer 3, already documented), AIDO-252 (the triggering incident).
notes: Linked to cross-repo hardening research: ai-harness AIH-764 (Research: systemic hardening against secret exposure into CC/agent session transcripts) -- related systemic gap (stale/missing secrets exposure via launcher not activating direnv), not the same failure shape as the other 5 tracked incidents but part of the same 'secrets handling keeps failing in new ways' pattern.

title: DONE 2026-07-23 — both bugs fixed for real, full suite green (1853 passed, 0 failed), no `SKIP_TESTS=1`.
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-121]` **DONE 2026-07-23 — both bugs fixed for real, full suite green (1853 passed, 0 failed), no `SKIP_TESTS=1`.** Two test-suite bugs surfaced by AI-CLI-120's fresh-worktree run. **Bug 1 (8 failures, `detect_repo_root()` "resolved to `.../.worktrees/...`" RuntimeError):** root cause was a **test bug, not a production bug** — `main.py`'s AI-CLI-99 repair backstop calls `_session.detect_repo_root()` for real, unmocked, before any of these 8 tests' own worktree-specific mocking begins; their blanket `subprocess.run` patches' generic "success, empty stdout" default fallback incidentally answers that unrelated call too. `detect_repo_root()` then treats `Path.cwd()` (with empty joined path) as the git-common-dir, and since the *real* pytest process cwd is inside a worktree, its parent naturally contains `.worktrees`, tripping the function's own worktree-nesting safety guard. Fixed by explicitly patching `ai_cli.session.detect_repo_root` to return `None` in all 8 affected tests (`tests/test_cli.py`, `TestCliWorktreeGitPull`'s shared `_run_c_with_fake_subprocess` helper plus 3 standalone tests in `TestCliSessionSetupBranches`/`TestCliSessionExecvp`) — `main.py` already handles a `None` return gracefully (skips the repair step), which is exactly the correct behavior for tests that aren't testing that code path at all. **Bug 2 (18 failures, Python-version drift):** fixed by adding `.python-version` (pinned to `3.13`) — no such pin existed anywhere in the repo, so a fresh worktree's `uv sync --frozen --extra dev` (no explicit `-p`) silently resolved to whatever uv's newest locally-installed interpreter was (3.14.3) instead of the fleet's actual working baseline (3.13.12); confirmed by deleting `.venv` and re-syncing with no override — now correctly resolves to 3.13 automatically. Verified: full suite (`uv run pytest -q`) — 1853 passed, 0 failed, 3 warnings (pre-existing, unrelated asyncio warnings) in ~11s. **Bug 3, found while re-verifying the push (17 failures + 9 errors, `git commit`/`git init` subprocess failures in temp fixture repos):** the suite ran clean under a manual `XDG_STATE_HOME=$(mktemp -d)` override but failed identically via the real pre-push test-gate hook, reproducing in two independently-fresh worktrees — proving it wasn't index corruption or worktree staleness. Root cause: no test-level isolation for `XDG_STATE_HOME` existed (only quota/Fable state had a dedicated fixture, `_isolate_quota_state`, AI-CLI-97) — tests creating ephemeral git repos raced against the real, shared `~/.local/state/ai-cli-utils/` whenever invoked without the manual override. Fixed with a new autouse fixture, `_isolate_xdg_state_home` (`tests/conftest.py`), isolating it for every test the same way quota state already was. Verified deterministic across 4 consecutive full-suite runs with no manual env override. **Bug 4, found re-verifying yet again (down to 4 `test_sync.py` failures, real git commit-message content bleeding into ephemeral `git commit` calls inside test fixtures, reproducing only via the real pre-commit-wrapped pre-push hook, never standalone):** root cause is `AI-CLI-70` itself, more precisely diagnosed this round — see `docs/bugs/worktree-index-corruption.md` Round 3. git injects `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` into every hook process; pre-commit strips these before its own internal git plumbing but not before running a hook's `entry` command (confirmed in pre-commit 4.6.0's `languages/unsupported_script.py`), so `test-gate.sh` and everything it spawns inherited the real worktree's git-targeting env raw. Fixed by stripping those vars at the top of `test-gate.sh` itself (canonical: `project-template@b0ef80a`, applied here at `39dfe6f`) — the earliest possible point of defense, ahead of pytest even starting. Verified: the push that had been failing on this exact leak succeeded cleanly on the next attempt with no other change. **Regression test added** (`tests/hooks/test-testgate-git-env-strip.sh`, matching the existing `tests/hooks/test-corrupt-index-guard.sh` convention): shims `git` on `PATH` to capture what env the first git subprocess `test-gate.sh` spawns actually sees, with leaked `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` simulated in the environment beforehand. RED-verified against a reverted copy of the fix (fails for the right reason — leaked vars visible) before being trusted GREEN against the real fixed script.

Fix Round 1: pre-push guard hook (`.githooks/corrupt-index-guard.sh`, 16 tests). Fix Round 2: self-healing in `main.py` before autostash runs (5 new tests). Fix Round 3: strip git-targeting env vars at the top of `test-gate.sh`, before pytest starts (canonical: `project-template@b0ef80a`, applied here `39dfe6f`). title: Bug: duplicate `/exit` injection in auto-restart watcher

Two root causes: (1) pane-content guard (`'^[[:space:]]*❯[[:space:]]*$'`) doesn't explicitly reject prompts that already contain `/exit` text; (2) `config_hash_file` is written once at session start and never updated after a config change is processed — so after `/exit` fires and CC restarts, the config change detector immediately re-fires because the stored hash is still the old one, creating a new `config_changed_file` → new `signal_file` → another injection. Fix: (a) add `/exit` content check before injection; (b) re-write `config_hash_file` with the current hash immediately after a config-triggered signal_file is created so the baseline advances. File: `src/ai_cli/session_script.py` ~lines 151–211. Related: `[AI-CLI-35]` (prompt injection safety), `[AI-CLI-74]` (auto-restart feature).

No grace-tuning fixes a fundamentally wrong mechanism. **Fix (robust, not a workaround):** CC 2.1.x runs slash commands non-interactively via `claude -p /usage` — deterministic (verified 3/3 incl. Fable, vs ~1/3), ~1-2s, and **$0** (`--output-format json` → `total_cost_usd:0`, zero tokens, `num_turns:0`; /usage is metadata, not a model turn). New `_get_usage_via_print_mode()` is now the primary path in `_get_claude_usage_snapshot()`; the legacy hidden-pane scrape is kept as a **fallback** only (belt-and-suspenders for CC versions where community docs still claim `-p` slash commands are interactive-only). title: Auto-register CC workspace trust at session/worktree launch (fix "workspace has not been trusted" permission drop)

Analysis: `ai-harness/docs/research/claude-code-workspace-trust-permission-drop.md`.

title: Root-cause + robustly fix the recurring `core.bare=true` git-config corruption from worktree operations
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-99]` **Root-cause + robustly fix the recurring `core.bare=true` git-config corruption from worktree operations** — DONE 2026-07-13. **Confirmed two vectors, fixed both:** (1) **leaked `GIT_*` env** — `session.py`'s `create_worktree`/`cleanup_worktree` and `copier_update.py`'s isolated-worktree flow ran `git worktree add/remove` via `subprocess.run` with no `env=`, inheriting the caller's `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/etc. verbatim; when the caller is a nested CC session already inside a worktree, those vars can leak into a worktree op targeting the shared main-tree gitdir and write `core.bare`/`core.worktree` onto it; (2) **a wrong "restore `core.bare=true`" recovery workflow** that had propagated via session memory/resume messages only (no committed doc said this) — main tree is a normal working tree, never intentionally bare. **Fix shipped:** new `src/ai_cli/git_repair.py` — `_git_env()` strips `GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES/GIT_PREFIX/GIT_CONFIG/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` before every git subprocess call in `session.py`/`copier_update.py`/`main.py`'s launch path that touches repo/worktree structure (keeps innocuous `GIT_SSH*`/`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`/`GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*`); `repair_bare_worktree_config(repo_root)` is a deterministic backstop — asserts + repairs `core.bare`/`core.worktree` on a normal working tree regardless of source (covers paths we don't control, e.g. CC's own `isolation: worktree` tool), wired at `ai c N` session launch (`main.py`, before/after the launch's git ops) and before/after every worktree add/remove in `copier_update.py` + `session.py`. **Tests:** 8 new (`tests/test_git_repair.py` — env-scrub incl. innocuous-var retention, repair for bare-only/stale-worktree-only/both/healthy-noop, plus a real-git-repo end-to-end repro of the exact corruption). Full suite 1811 passed, ruff clean. **No live repro of the leak itself** (constructing the exact GIT_* combination that reproduces the write proved not deterministic in isolation — see ai-harness `docs/research/nested-agent-worktree-orchestration.md` § root-cause note); the env-scrub + backstop guard are correct regardless of the precise trigger. Research: [📄 ai-harness/docs/research/nested-agent-worktree-orchestration.md](../../../ai-harness/docs/research/nested-agent-worktree-orchestration.md) § "Root cause + fix — `core.bare=true` recurrence". Also resolves the guard referenced prospectively as AIH-215 in ai-harness plan docs (no separate AIH-215 roadmap entry existed — this AI-CLI-99 fix is that guard). Related: AIH-167, AI-CLI-89, AI-CLI-91, #182. **Deploy:** reinstall in 3 places (local Mac `uv tool install`, Hetzner `uv tool install`, aido venv `uv pip install`) — handled by the launching session, not this task.

title: Windows CI matrix comprehensively broken -- ~100 test failures across nearly every test file, root cause unscoped
description:
The test-windows CI job (Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 on windows-latest) has been failing on every main run for 24+ hours (checked back 15 runs to 08-15 05:06Z, all red). This is not a small bug -- roughly 100 individual test failures span nearly every test file (test_cli.py, test_session.py, test_remote.py, test_iterm2.py, test_sync.py, test_quota.py, test_workspace.py, test_growthbook_launch_toggle.py, test_copier_update.py, test_bare_worktree.py, and more). Recurring patterns observed: POSIX-only stdlib attributes assumed present (os.getuid, os.ttyname missing on frozen Windows os module), path-separator mismatches (backslash vs forward-slash comparisons), UnicodeEncodeError/UnicodeDecodeError (cp1252/charmap default encoding vs UTF-8 assumptions), execvp/Popen mock call assertions failing (0 calls expected 1, suggesting a Windows-specific code path that never reaches the mocked call), and tmux-dependent tests failing (README documents tmux as explicitly unsupported on Windows, so these may need a skip guard rather than a fix). README claims Windows is a supported platform via MSYS2 + Git Bash, so this is a real, currently-unaddressed gap between that claim and CI reality -- not obviously a recent regression (need to confirm how long this job has been broken; may predate recent work entirely).

This issue is scoped as RESEARCH FIRST, not a blind fix attempt (Sergei's explicit call, 2026-08-16): investigate and categorize the ~100 failures into causal buckets (missing POSIX-API guards, path-separator bugs, encoding bugs, mock/assertion issues specific to Windows code paths, tests that should be platform-skipped like the tmux ones), estimate the scope/cost of a real fix for each bucket, and produce a short root-cause + scoping writeup (not a full fix) so a follow-up decision can be made: fix incrementally, mark test-windows as continue-on-error until fixed, or descope Windows support entirely if the gap turns out to be structural.

title: ai session-adopt — fails when session ran in worktree (searches repo-root CC slug instead of worktree slug)
ai c silently resumes the wrong (older, unrelated) session when the intended most-recent one is a live background agent
description:
Observed live 2026-08-12 (sergei's own machine, sw-6 fleet-coordinator session in the sergei repo worktree sw-6). A live interactive session (session id e708efd4-bdb7-4a55-a1c8-997e9747adc8, custom title sw-6) was exited normally by the user (intending to relaunch in bypass-permissions mode) but did not actually terminate -- it was instead left running as a detached background agent process. The user then ran `ai c 6` to relaunch, expecting it to continue that same fleet-coordinator conversation. Instead it silently landed on a completely different, unrelated older transcript (session id e2184270-60ed-44f2-b198-3b16abfa6dc3, an ad-hoc research conversation about Israeli-Palestinian negotiations) with no warning that the intended/expected session was unavailable.

Root cause (confirmed): `claude --continue` cannot resume a session that is already running live (confirmed via `claude --resume <id>` returning "Session <id> is currently running as a background agent (bg). Use `claude agents` to find and attach to it, or add --fork-session to branch off a copy."). Because the correct, most-recently-used session was busy, `ai c`'s continue-resolution silently fell back to the NEXT most recent transcript for that cwd instead -- with zero indication to the user that this happened. The user spent an extended troubleshooting session (with an assisting Claude Code instance) trying `-r`/`--resume` (which is `ai c`'s own tmux-reattach flag, unrelated to Claude Code's own session resume), the native `/resume` picker (worked, but required manually identifying the correct session by custom title among only 2 candidates), and finally `claude --resume <id>` directly (which surfaced the real root cause: the session was still alive as a background agent).

Two distinct problems to fix, potentially separable:
1. (ai-cli-utils, `ai c`'s launch/continue-resolution logic) When the most-recently-used transcript for a cwd cannot be resumed because it is a currently-running background agent, `ai c` should say so explicitly (e.g. "most recent session <name> is running as a background agent; falling back to <next-session-name>, or run `claude agents` to attach to it directly") rather than silently substituting a different, unrelated conversation with no warning.
2. (Possibly Claude Code itself, or a documentation/procedure gap) A session the user believed they cleanly exited was instead left running as an orphaned background agent -- worth understanding whether this is expected behavior from some launch flag/mode combination (e.g. bypass-permissions relaunch flow) or a genuine leak.

Both a Claude Code CLI /bug-report AND this internal bug doc were discussed; the CC-native bug-report flow requires explicit user invocation (locked from model-invocation per AIH-876) and has not yet been filed by the user. This doc captures the ai-cli-utils-side finding and reproduction for that separate track.
notes: Resolved AI-CLI-210 (commit 902581c on main): ai c now detects title-matched live Claude Code sessions via the local session registry (~/.claude/sessions/*.json, matched by sessionId), avoids touching or continuing them, warns with title+pid and recovery steps (claude agents / --fork-session), and starts a fresh session instead. The tmux path now delegates to the same Python resolver via a new 'ai internal resolve-continue-target' subcommand, removing the prior duplicate/buggy inline implementation. Full suite: 2309 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated tmux-server flake (confirmed not a regression -- passes in isolation with and without the diff). Problem #2 from the bug doc (why the original session didn't terminate cleanly) remains open, out of scope, tracked separately per the doc.

title: Newly created worktree/session/CC title inherit the fleet-registry prefix casing verbatim instead of always lowercasing
description:
Follow-up to AI-CLI-206 (AI-CLI-565q, fixed at commit 2519721). That fix
covers RESUMING an existing worktree/session when the current invocation's
prefix casing or remote-marker differs from what's already on disk/in tmux.

It does NOT cover the other half: when there is no existing slot to resume
and a genuinely NEW worktree/session/CC custom-title is created, the name is
still built verbatim from resolve_project_prefix()'s registry value
(session.py get_project_prefix(), consumed by build_session_name()). If a
project's registered fleet prefix is uppercase (as fleet-registry prefixes
conventionally are, e.g. for beads task ids), the new worktree directory,
tmux session name, and CC session's customTitle (iTerm2 tab/window title via
ai_name) all come out uppercase too -- e.g. worktree ".worktrees/APP-8",
tmux "c-APP-8", title "APP-8".

The user's stated expectation: only the beads task-id prefix should ever be
uppercase. The CC session, its custom title, and the worktree directory name
should always be lowercase, regardless of the casing registered in the fleet
registry for bd task-id purposes.

ROOT CAUSE (needs verification, not just trusted): get_project_prefix()
(session.py ~line 237) returns resolve_project_prefix()'s value verbatim,
and its own docstring already states "Worktree names and custom session
titles are both built from this value" -- so the fix likely belongs at that
single choke point (lowercase there, or at each of build_session_name()'s
three call sites in main.py), NOT in resolve_project_prefix() itself, which
must keep returning the registry's canonical casing untouched for any
current or future bd-task-id-prefix consumer. Confirmed this session:
ai_name/session_id from build_session_name() flow directly into
_iterm2._emit_iterm2_profile_setup() (main.py ~2192), which sets the CC
customTitle/tab title -- so build_session_name() is the single choke point.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A newly created worktree directory name is always lowercase, regardless of
  the fleet-registry prefix's registered casing.
- A newly created tmux session name is always lowercase (except the engine
  tag c/g and the -r- remote marker, which are already lowercase).
- The CC session's customTitle (iTerm2 tab/pane title, set from ai_name) is
  always lowercase.
- resolve_project_prefix()/get_project_prefix()'s return value is UNCHANGED
  (still returns the registry's literal casing) -- lowercasing happens only
  at the point(s) where the value feeds worktree/session/title naming, not
  at the source.
- No regression to AI-CLI-206's fix (case-insensitive resume matching must
  keep working for a legacy uppercase worktree/session that predates this
  fix).
- Regression test: a fleet-registry prefix registered uppercase; a brand
  new session launch (no pre-existing worktree/session for that slot);
  asserts the resulting worktree dir, tmux session name, and ai_name/title
  are all lowercase.
close_reason: Fixed and independently verified across 2 audit rounds at commit acf7ab4: newly created worktree/tmux-session/CC-title now always lowercase, resolve_project_prefix()/get_project_prefix() unchanged for other consumers, AI-CLI-206 resume matching unaffected. Round 1 (Codex audit, high effort) found 8 issues including a real shell-injection vector (F-1, unquoted remote prefix reaching a remote shell command) -- all 8 fixed and independently re-verified against the audit's own reproduction commands. Round 2 (fresh Codex audit) confirmed 7/8 fixes PASS; fixed the 1 trivial P3 (N-2, docstring) directly; deferred 1 P1 (N-1, remote named-session preview identity mismatch) to AI-CLI-209 after verifying it predates this fix entirely (pre-existing at commit 2519721^, unrelated to casing). Full audit trail: docs/audits/ai-cli-208-session-naming-casing-audit.md.

description:

created or reused (e.g. return a (path, created: bool) tuple, or check

by Codex audit Round 2 (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md,

title: ruff-check pre-commit runs --fix, so widening select would mass-autofix unreviewed
description:
The `ruff-check` pre-commit hook runs with `args: [--fix]` (.pre-commit-config.yaml:62, verified 2026-08-06). That is fine for the current narrow rule set, which reports "All checks passed!" — there is nothing left to fix. It becomes a defect the moment `[tool.ruff.lint] select` is widened.

THE MECHANISM. Widening `select` is not a neutral config edit while `--fix` is on. Newly-selected families do not surface as a reviewable list of findings; they get AUTOFIXED, file by file, inside whatever unrelated commits happen to touch those files next. So a rule-set change lands as scattered mechanical edits across many commits, attributed to whoever was working on something else, with nobody ever reviewing it as a change.

WHY THAT IS THE WRONG WAY ROUND. The tracked lint-adoption work carries an explicit constraint: do NOT bulk-autofix, because the concern is a mass mechanical change nobody reviews. But `--fix` does not prevent the autofix, it only removes the review. One deliberate, reviewable commit that applies a phase's fixes in full is strictly BETTER than the same edits dribbling through unrelated commits. The constraint as written protects against the visible version of the problem while the invisible version is already wired in.

MEASURED CONTEXT (2026-08-06, this repo, `ruff check --select <F> --statistics src/ tests/`):
  current select E4,E7,E9,F -> All checks passed (0)
  phase-1 candidates I,UP  -> 229 findings, 228 of them autofixable
So the very first adoption phase is ~99.6% autofixable, which is exactly the case where `--fix` would silently do all the work before anyone looked at it.

Note also that the finding counts alone mislead about scope, which is a separate reason to want the diff reviewable: SIM's 441 findings are 375x SIM117 (stacked `patch()` in tests), and PLC's 513 are 512x PLC0415 (deliberate lazy imports, which that rule's own documentation concedes as legitimate). A family total is not a work estimate.

WHAT THIS ISSUE IS NOT. It is not a proposal to adopt any rule family — that decision is tracked separately and is the user's call. It is also not a claim that `--fix` is wrong in general; for a stable rule set it is a convenience with no downside. The defect is specifically the interaction: `--fix` plus a widening `select` equals an unreviewed mass rewrite.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Widening `select` cannot cause unreviewed mechanical rewrites. Either `--fix` is removed from the hook, or an equivalent mechanism ensures a newly-selected family's fixes land as one deliberate reviewable change rather than piecemeal through unrelated commits.

AC-2 Whatever the mechanism, `ruff check` still FAILS the hook on a genuine violation. A fix that makes the hook merely report and pass would be worse than the current state — prove the hook still blocks a commit that introduces a violation.

AC-3 FAILURE PATH: prove the unreviewed-rewrite scenario is actually closed. With the new arrangement, add a rule family to `select`, then commit an unrelated one-line edit to a file carrying findings from that family, and assert the commit does NOT silently rewrite that file. This must be demonstrated, not argued — the current behavior and the fixed behavior look identical on a clean tree, so a probe on a clean tree proves nothing.

AC-4 The developer experience is documented: whoever adopts a phase should have a stated, discoverable way to apply that phase's fixes on purpose (an explicit `ruff check --fix` invocation is fine — the point is that it is deliberate and reviewable, not automatic).

AC-5 Do not adopt, widen, or narrow any rule family as part of this fix. Config scope stays exactly as it is; only the autofix behavior changes.

CONTEXT. Surfaced 2026-08-06 by the lint rule-set selection research (docs/research/ruff-ruleset-selection.md), which flagged it as its own open question after finding the hook's `--fix` flag. Nothing in the original lint-adoption issue anticipated it. Independently verified at .pre-commit-config.yaml:62. This is a PREREQUISITE for any rule-set widening, so it should be resolved before the first adoption phase, not after.

title: ai session-audit: survey titled CC sessions fleet-wide and drive adoption reproducibly
description:
`ai session-adopt` (AI-CLI-168, shipped 2026-08-06) adopts ONE named session per invocation, and `-a/--all` only sweeps titled sessions inside a single source directory. There is no way to answer, or to act on, the fleet-wide question: "which titled CC sessions exist anywhere, where does each one actually live, and which are not resumable by `ai c <n>` from their repo root?"

That gap cost real time on 2026-08-06. Doing the AI-CLI-151 adoptions by hand required an ad hoc Python one-liner over `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` to extract `customTitle` per transcript, plus manual cross-referencing against `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` for liveness and against each repo's `.worktrees/` for the destination. Two concrete defects surfaced only because of that manual survey:

1. **A recorded location was simply wrong.** Both AI-CLI-151 and AI-CLI-168 stated that `aih-1` lived at the ai-harness repo ROOT. It did not — the root transcript is `aih-2`. `aih-1` was in `.claude/worktrees/aih-657-profile-correction`, an AGENT worktree. A title-based adopt from the repo root failed with "no transcript titled 'aih-1'" until `-s/--source` was pointed at the real directory. Nothing in the tooling could have surfaced that; it took a hand-rolled scan.

2. **A title collision was invisible until adopt refused it.** Two transcripts both claimed `kg-3` (419 lines at the kg repo root, 2708 lines in `.worktrees/kg-3`). The collision gate correctly refused and proposed a free index, but there was no way to see the collision coming, or to see that it was the only one, without scanning every project directory by hand.

MEASURED FLEET STATE (2026-08-06, this machine): 187 transcripts total, 11 titled. After the AI-CLI-151 adoptions all 11 titles are unique fleet-wide and 0 collisions remain. Titled sessions: aih-1, aih-2, aih-3, acto-1, aido-1, ai-cli-1, kg-1, kg-2, kg-3, kg-4, proj-1.

WHY A COMMAND AND NOT A ONE-OFF SCRIPT. This is not a migration that happens once. New sessions are started outside `ai c` continuously (a plain `claude` in a repo root, a CC agent worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`), so the fleet drifts back out of adoption on its own. The survey is also the natural place to catch the two failure modes above BEFORE an adopt is attempted, rather than discovering them from a refusal. A reproducible command with explicit options for where to look and what to do is the difference between re-deriving the survey by hand every time and running one thing.

SCOPE NOTE. This is the SURVEY-AND-DRIVE half. The adoption mechanics already exist in `session_adopt.py` and must be REUSED, not reimplemented. In particular the unconditional title-collision gate must keep working exactly as it does now: it is the safety property that prevented a nondeterministic `ai c` resolve, and `-y/--yes` must never cover it. The live-session refusal must likewise stay intact — adopting a live session moves a transcript out from under a running CC process. Note both live-session and collision refusals are CORRECT behavior, so a bulk driver must report them as expected outcomes and continue, never treat them as errors to work around.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 A new `ai` subcommand surveys titled CC sessions across the fleet and reports, per session: the title, the transcript path, its line count, the repo the transcript's cwd belongs to, whether it is already in the correct worktree slot, whether it is currently live, and whether `ai c <n>` resolves it from its repo root.

AC-2 The survey discovers sessions in ALL the places they actually occur, not just repo roots: repo roots, `.worktrees/<name>`, and CC agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/<id>`. The `aih-1` case above must appear correctly, attributed to ai-harness, without the caller supplying its path.

AC-3 The command reports title collisions (one title claimed by more than one transcript) as a distinct, named condition, with every claimant listed, BEFORE any adoption is attempted.

AC-4 The command has an option to drive adoption for everything it finds that is safe to adopt, delegating to the existing `session_adopt` code path rather than duplicating it.

AC-5 A dry-run option shows exactly what would happen and writes nothing. Verify by asserting the filesystem is byte-identical before and after a dry run, not merely by reading the output.

AC-6 Options exist to control WHERE it looks and WHAT it acts on (at minimum: restrict to one repo, and restrict to one title), so the command is usable narrowly and not only as a whole-fleet sweep.

AC-7 FAILURE PATH: when a session is live, or its title collides, the command reports that session as skipped with the specific reason and a non-zero-signal in the summary, continues processing the remaining sessions, and does NOT adopt the refused one. A refusal for one session must never abort the batch.

title: session-adopt live-session refusal is proven with os.getpid(), not a real CC process
description:
`ai session-adopt` refuses to adopt a session that is currently live, which is correct and necessary: adopting a live session would move the transcript out from under a running CC process. But the test that proves the refusal works uses `os.getpid()` — the pytest process's own PID — as the stand-in for a live session, rather than a real Claude Code process.

WHY THAT IS WEAK. The refusal path reads the session registry (`~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`) and checks liveness. Using the test runner's own PID proves only that "some live PID is detected", not that the code correctly identifies a live *CC* session from a real registry entry with a real `name`/`sessionId`/`cwd` payload. A regression that changed which field the liveness check keys on, or that stopped reading the registry at all and fell back to a bare PID probe, could keep this test green while the real refusal silently stopped working. That is the failure mode that matters, because the consequence is moving a transcript out from under a running session.

Probe adequacy: the current test would print the same PASS whether the registry lookup works or is bypassed entirely. Pass and fail are indistinguishable, which is the tell.

CONTEXT. Surfaced 2026-08-06 as the one open item on AI-CLI-168 after `ai session-adopt` shipped (module `src/ai_cli/session_adopt.py`, 784 lines, 100% coverage, no pragma). It was carried as an open sub-item of 168, which then blocked AI-CLI-151 from closing even though all four adoptions were verified complete. Splitting it out so the adoption work can close and this keeps its own identity.

The refusal itself is BELIEVED CORRECT and is not known to be broken — this is about the strength of its proof, not a reported defect. Do not "fix" the refusal without first reproducing a real failure.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 The live-session refusal is exercised against a realistic registry entry: a `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` payload with a real-shaped `name`, `sessionId` and `cwd`, in a redirected/tmp session dir, not the real one.

AC-2 The PID used is a process the test itself owns and reaps, not the pytest process. Per the fleet test rule: spawn with `start_new_session=True`, reap the process GROUP with `os.killpg`, escalate SIGTERM then SIGKILL, and assume the cleanup path may not run.

AC-3 A negative control: with the registry entry absent (or naming a dead PID), the same adoption SUCCEEDS. Without this the test cannot distinguish "refused because live" from "refused for any reason".

AC-4 The test must fail if the liveness check is removed or made to always-return-not-live. Prove it by breaking the check and watching it go red, per the fleet guard rule.

AC-5 Do not weaken or remove the refusal to make testing easier. Adopting a live session stays refused.

title: TestQuotaStatuslinePart flakes ~1 run in 4 under xdist because it derives its clock from the real wall time
description:
tests/test_quota.py::TestQuotaStatuslinePart fails nondeterministically under the full suite with xdist, at roughly 1 run in 4. Two DIFFERENT tests in that class have been observed failing across runs, which is the signature of a timing dependency rather than a broken assertion.

ROOT CAUSE. The tests derive fixed_now from qdb._get_current_week_start(), which reads the real wall clock. Two calls within a single run can land on opposite sides of a week boundary, so the fixture's timing premise shifts underneath the assertions and no rows match the window being queried. The statusline then renders its placeholder instead of the recorded percentage, and the test fails.

EVIDENCE, from two independent agents that each hit it while working on unrelated tasks:
- Reproduced on a PRISTINE stash of the in-flight work, so it is not caused by any current change.
- Never fails when test_quota.py runs alone: 149 passed, three consecutive runs. It needs full-suite timing to surface.
- Measured 1 failure across 4 consecutive full-suite runs.
- A separate agent independently hit the same class from a different angle: tests there were writing the REAL user file ~/.local/state/ai-cli/quota-reset-anchor.txt because _get_reset_anchor_path() was never redirected, so one xdist worker's write moved another worker's week boundary. That specific leak is already fixed (the quota-isolation fixture now redirects it, alongside the DB and backoff file it already handled). This issue is the REMAINING half: even with the anchor isolated, deriving the clock from datetime.now() at test time is still a race against the real week boundary.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN PASSING. AI-CLI-158 is already active work on hermeticity in this same test class, so an unrelated task editing it risks a conflict. Flagging rather than silently tolerating it: "pre-existing" is a diagnosis, not a sign-off.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 The class no longer reads the real wall clock. Inject week_start and now explicitly rather than deriving them from datetime.now() inside the test.

AC-2 The full suite passes 10 consecutive times with xdist enabled. One green run does not clear a 1-in-4 flake, so the check has to be repeated enough to be meaningful.

AC-3 A test asserts the clock is actually frozen, so the injection cannot silently stop applying and let the flake back in.

AC-4 Coordinate with AI-CLI-158 rather than editing around it, since both touch the same class.

AC-5 Do not paper over it by serializing the file or marking it xfail. The point is a hermetic clock, not a suppressed symptom.

CONTEXT. Surfaced 2026-08-06 during the AI-CLI-168 session-adopt build, by two separate agents. Same family as the anchor-file leak that was fixed in that work: shared mutable state under parallel test execution.
close_reason: Fixed in the merge of fa4b45d/978c063/1921a3d. TWO coupled defects: (1) tests/conftest.py never redirected _get_reset_anchor_path(), so the suite wrote the REAL user file ~/.local/state/ai-cli/quota-reset-anchor.txt, and since that anchor sets the quota week, one xdist worker moved another workers boundary; (2) TestQuotaStatuslinePart derived fixed_now from the real clock twice per run, and two acceleration-arrow tests never froze it at all. Both fixed, plus the same pattern in the single-line contract helper. IMPORTANT ON VERIFICATION: 10 consecutive green runs were obtained AND THEN SHOWN INADMISSIBLE, because pristine origin/main also passed the same harness 4/4 -- the 1-in-4 rate depends on the real anchor files current value, which had converged to a self-consistent now+2d. That is very likely why several earlier reported passes in this repo could not be reproduced. The admissible probe amplifies the same mechanism (a concurrent writer rewriting the anchor every 2ms, alternating the two values the suite itself writes): pre-fix 9 failed/147 passed across multiple tests with the exact reported symptom, post-fix 158 passed. I re-verified independently: 2114 passed, and a sentinel seeded into the real anchor file SURVIVED a full suite run (it was overwritten before the fix). Also fixes test_env_throttle_skips_duplicate_snapshot, which was failing DETERMINISTICALLY here (assert 2 == 1) because the leaked anchor split its snapshots across weeks -- so the previously reported 2112 baseline was itself contingent on that leaked file holding a compatible value. Two new frozen-clock guards each carry a positive control so they cannot pass vacuously. No xfail, skip, serialization, retry plugin, or pragma added.

title: ai copier-update silently drops a patch hunk (false success) when target-repo content has drifted from template anchor lines
description:
Discovered 2026-08-02 while propagating a one-line .gitignore addition
(.claude/.rc-pair-state.json) from project-template to the fleet via ai copier-update
(AIH-586/CORE-135's sibling task). 10 of 20 repos reported "updated + pushed" but their
.gitignore was never actually touched -- verified independently: acn-automation's pushed
commit (83f0f9a7) is a 1-line .copier-answers.yml _commit bump only, no .gitignore change,
even though the tool reported success and the _commit ref correctly advanced to the new
project-template commit.

Root cause (as diagnosed by the delegated worker, not yet independently re-derived from
copier's own source): each affected repo's real .gitignore has locally drifted around the
patch's anchor lines (e.g. extra entries like .gemini/no_jira_required or
.claude/debug_confirmed inserted nearby, or scheduled_tasks.lock relocated away from
no_jira_required) -- copier's 3-way diff/patch can't find matching context and silently
drops that hunk rather than raising it as a conflict. The tool's own "updated + pushed"
report is therefore not a reliable signal that the intended file content actually landed --
it only reflects the _commit ref advancing and SOME hunk (often just .copier-answers.yml
itself) applying cleanly.

Impact: any future propagation of a change to a file that individual repos commonly
customize (gitignore, pre-commit config, etc.) is at risk of silently not landing in some
subset of repos while reporting full success. This was only caught here because of an
explicit follow-up content-grep verification step -- copier-update's own reporting alone
would have missed it entirely.

Not fixed here -- filed for follow-up triage/fix. See sibling finding filed separately in
project-template for the 8 repos where a REAL (correctly-flagged) conflict exists due to
unrelated pre-commit-config template drift, and a second sibling finding for 2 repos
(ai-dojo, ai-ide-macos) where copier's internal checkout step fails outright on an
unrelated pathspec error.
acceptance_criteria:
- ai copier-update (or the copier invocation it wraps) either surfaces a dropped-hunk as a
  conflict/warning instead of silent success, or the wrapper adds a post-apply verification
  step that diffs each changed template file's actual expected content against the target
  repo's file before reporting "updated + pushed".
- A regression test reproduces the silent-drop condition (a target repo with drifted context
  around a template anchor line) and confirms it is now surfaced, not silently swallowed.

title: uv tool install warns 'Failed to hardlink files; falling back to full copy' on every ai update — cache and tool dir are on different filesystems
description:
Every 'ai update' (and the auto-update that runs at 'ai c N' launch) prints:

  warning: Failed to hardlink files; falling back to full copy. This may lead to degraded performance.
           If the cache and target directories are on different filesystems, hardlinking may not be supported.
           If this is intentional, set 'export UV_LINK_MODE=copy' or use '--link-mode=copy' to suppress this warning.

Root cause (measured, not inferred): uv's cache and its tool-install target are on DIFFERENT filesystems, so hardlinking is physically impossible and uv falls back to copying.
  - uv cache dir  = ~/user-default-efs/caches/uv  -> st_dev 60,    nfs4 (EFS mount)
  - tool root     = ~/.local/share/uv/tools       -> st_dev 66308, xfs (local NVMe)
  - UV_CACHE_DIR is exported from ~/.bashrc to the EFS path.

Call site: src/ai_cli/main.py:1240 builds [uv, 'tool', 'install', project_path, '--force'] with no --link-mode. Also relevant: 'uv tool upgrade' at main.py:450 and main.py:2150.

The warning is cosmetic (the install succeeds and is correct) but it fires on every single update on any machine whose uv cache is on a different mount than its tool dir — noisy, and it trains the user to ignore update output. Not machine-specific in principle: any split-mount layout hits it (containers, NFS/EFS homes, separate /home volume).

Proposed fix: detect the st_dev mismatch between uv's resolved cache dir and the tool install dir, and pass --link-mode=copy only when they differ. Do not hardcode copy mode unconditionally — that would discard the hardlink fast path on normal single-filesystem machines. Must be cross-platform (Windows/macOS/Linux); os.stat().st_dev works on all three.
close_reason: Root cause: uv cache dir and tool-install dir on different filesystems (different st_dev) -> hardlink impossible -> uv falls back to copy and warns. Fix: resolve uv's own cache/install dirs, compare st_dev, pass --link-mode=copy only when they differ; never hardcoded (preserves hardlink fast path on single-fs machines); any resolution/stat failure falls through to prior behavior. Wired into all 4 call sites (update, background auto-update, ai upgrade, extra_venvs pip install). Verified LIVE with negative control: warning present without flag, absent with it; real 'ai update' now clean. Installed build verified by content (5 occurrences). Suite 2009 passed / 0 skipped; ruff clean. Commit aa8a247. Doc: docs/bugs/uv-hardlink-fallback-warning.md (BUG-008).

title: Investigate the 7 permanently-skipped tests: justified or masking real gaps?

title: ruff 0.16.0 pin surfaced ~734 pre-existing violations; any commit touching those files is blocked
description:
Measured 2026-07-27 on ai-cli-utils at 36ec6b6, ruff 0.16.0 (the AIH-473 pin):

  pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files
  -> Found 1199 errors (465 fixed automatically, 734 remaining)

  ruff check .        -> 1074 errors
  ruff check src/     ->  491 errors

SCOPE - read this before panicking or before "fixing" it with a bulk auto-fix:

The repo is NOT frozen. pre-commit runs against STAGED files, not --all-files, so a commit
touching only clean files passes; two commits landed tonight (08e8471, 36ec6b6) after the
pin. What IS blocked is any commit touching one of the files carrying a violation - which
is how this will actually be discovered, one contributor at a time.

A sub-agent independently reported "518 in src/ai_cli/" earlier the same evening; the live
number is 491 because the repo advanced. Directionally the same finding, and it is real -
I reproduced it rather than relaying it.

WHY NOW: AIH-473 pinned ruff to 0.16.0 fleet-wide. 0.16.0's default ruleset is stricter
than what this repo was previously linted against, so these are pre-existing violations
newly surfaced by the pin, not new defects introduced by anyone's code.

DO NOT bulk-apply `ruff check --fix` and commit it. I ran the hook exploratorily and it
auto-modified 60 files in the main tree in one shot; I reverted it. 465 unreviewed
mechanical rewrites across production modules (main.py, session.py, transport.py,
process_manager.py, ...) is not a reviewable diff, and this repo is on the critical path -
ai-cli is the session launcher for the whole fleet, deployed in 3 places.

SUGGESTED SHAPE: fix per-module in reviewable batches, in a WORKTREE not the main tree,
running the real gate (pre-commit run ruff-check --files <paths>) rather than bare ruff,
with the full 1901-test suite green per batch. Start with whatever modules are under
active edit so contributors stop hitting it.

unbounded-retry hang).

comments.author: Sergei Wallace
comments.text:
New finding (2026-07-28, sem-kg machine): the .venv does not contain the pinned ruff at all -- .venv/bin/python -m ruff --version reports 0.15.11, while pyproject.toml [dependency-groups] pins ruff==0.16.0 (two places, lines 64 and 73) and .pre-commit-config.yaml pins the same.

This explains the confusing split symptom that led here: the documented hard gate 'ruff check src/ tests/' passes CLEAN on 0.15.11, so a contributor following the documented workflow sees a green gate, while pre-commit's own pinned 0.16.0 binary reports the ~1073 errors this issue tracks. Same repo, same command, two different verdicts depending on which binary resolves -- so 'the gate passed' currently proves nothing about whether a commit will survive the hook.

A delegated agent hit this and had to commit with SKIP=ruff-check to make progress. Measured independently on this machine: pyproject pin 0.16.0 vs venv 0.15.11 confirmed by reading both.

Implication for this issue's scope: the version skew is arguably the more urgent half. Until the venv matches its own pin, any contributor's local ruff result is untrustworthy, and the violation count cannot be verified from inside the venv. Suggest the fix order be (1) sync the venv to the pin so the gate tells the truth, then (2) work the violations per the existing DO-NOT-bulk-autofix guidance above.

comments.author: Sergei Wallace
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE of the "1075 violations" is narrower than this bead's framing, and it changes what needs fixing.

[tool.ruff.lint] declared "ignore" but never "select", so the gate enforced whatever the resolved ruff binary's DEFAULT ruleset happened to be. Ruff 0.16.0 changed that default from 61 rules to 415.

Decisive measurement (.venv/bin/python -m ruff, version confirmed 0.16.0 from that same binary, 2026-07-28 ~20:30 UTC):
  findings under 0.16.0's inherited default:            1075
  findings inside E4/E7/E9/F (families ever selected):     0

All 1075 come from families the repo never opted into (SIM 369, PLW 151, BLE 147, UP 107, S 83, I 77, plus ASYNC B C DTZ FLY FURB ISC PIE PLR RUF TRY). And all three existing "ignore" entries (E701/E702/E741) are E7 codes, which only makes sense under select = E4,E7,E9,F.

Proof that the select reconstructs the historical set exactly, not approximately:
  0.15.11 stock defaults        -> 59 rule codes
  0.16.0 with select E4,E7,E9,F -> 59 rule codes
  diff                          -> IDENTICAL

FIXED on branch worktree-agent-a1454e956027bfbb2 (commit fa99eb0), NOT pushed:
- pyproject.toml declares select = E4,E7,E9,F -> the documented gate returns to exit 0
- check_installed_version() added to the ruff-version-sync hook: compares the pin to the ruff ACTUALLY INSTALLED, not just pre-commit rev vs pyproject pin (both were already 0.16.0 and passed throughout the defect). Resolves the venv explicitly, never via PATH.
- test-time version assertion, because the failure seen in practice was "measured, then it changed underneath", not "wrong version installed"
- CONTRIBUTING.md gate corrected to "uv run ruff check ..." (a bare ruff has no sync step)
- docs/bugs/ruff-gate-inherited-ruleset.md (BUG-006)

Guard proven able to fail: two real venvs, identical repo files -> 0.16.0 exit 0, 0.15.11 exit 1, no ruff exit 1. A real downgrade of the live venv turns both version tests red.

STILL OPEN, and this bead remains the right home for it: whether to ADOPT any of the new families (SIM/BLE/PLW/UP/S/I), in what order, and whether to raise the gate to --all-files afterwards. Nothing was auto-fixed; the no-bulk-fix decision stands. 417 of the 1075 are auto-fixable.

NOTE for anyone reading the earlier venv-skew measurements: "stat .venv/bin/ruff" cannot date the install. That path is a hardlink into the uv cache (links=5), so its mtime is the cache download time and reads identically whether the venv was provisioned an hour ago or a minute ago. Use .venv/lib/*/site-packages/ruff-*.dist-info/RECORD (links=1) instead.

title: ai update --force silently converts an editable tool install into a copy
description:
Found 2026-07-27 during the AI-CLI-134 three-place deploy, by an agent checking its own work
rather than trusting exit codes.

MECHANISM: _do_update_or_deploy runs uv tool install with no --editable flag. On the Mac,
ai-cli-utils is deliberately installed EDITABLE (PEP 610 direct_url.json shows editable true), so
the installed code IS the checkout and a git pull updates it. Running ai update --force silently
replaces that with a non-editable COPY. Nothing warns; the command exits 0.

WHY IT MATTERS: the editable posture is what makes a Mac git pull sufficient. Once converted to a
copy, the install silently rots on every subsequent pull, and the drift is invisible until someone
diffs installed bytes against the checkout. That is exactly the failure mode of AI-CLI-137, where
the aido venv sat 12 of 28 files stale for 12 days undetected.

CAUGHT ONLY BECAUSE the agent re-read direct_url.json after installing. "The command exited 0" did
not catch it and would never have.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY, it is intentional and must be preserved: Hetzner installs ai-cli-utils as a
COPY on purpose (editable false), so the fix is not "always pass --editable". It is to preserve
whatever posture the install already had, or to make the posture explicit and refuse to change it
silently.
acceptance_criteria: ai update preserves an existing install's editable-vs-copy posture, or refuses to change it without saying so. A test asserts the posture is unchanged across an update, for both the editable (Mac) and copy (Hetzner) cases.

title: Auto-clean stale worktrees and branches that carry no unique work
description:
CC sessions reliably forget to remove a worktree after merging its branch to main. The debris accumulates silently and is only noticed when someone audits.

Measured 2026-07-27: 31 local branches across 6 repos had ZERO unique commits vs origin/main and no worktree attached. All 31 were safe-deleted with 'git branch -d' (zero refusals). Breakdown: sergei 14, ai-harness 10, ai-cli-utils 4, ai-ide-mobile 1, artelier 1, aurion 1.

The shape of the debris matters for the design: 22 of the 31 were sub-agent isolation leftovers ('agent-*' / 'worktree-agent-*'), nearly all from the preceding three days. So the dominant producer is not human forgetfulness on 'ai c' worktrees -- it is EVERY delegated sub-agent leaving a branch behind once its work merges. Any cleanup that only handles 'ai c' worktrees will miss the majority of the problem.

Filed in ai-cli-utils rather than ai-harness or ai-core because the 'ai' CLI already owns the adjacent surfaces: 'ai ws pull' walks every worktree in the workspace file (and just gained upstream-drift reporting under AI-CLI-128), and 'ai ps clean' establishes the cleanup-command precedent. ai-harness owns context and hooks, not fleet git operations. Note the cleanup must ALSO handle CC-native '.claude/worktrees/agent-*' trees, which ai-cli-utils does not create -- see AIH-450.

Design constraints learned today, not optional:
1. Safety must come from git, not from our own containment logic. 'git branch -d' refuses a branch that is not fully merged; that refusal IS the safety property. Do not reimplement the check and then call 'git branch -D'.
2. Age alone is not a safety signal. A three-day-old branch can hold the only copy of real work. Zero-unique-commits is the necessary condition; age is at most a secondary filter to avoid racing active work.
3. A worktree whose directory still exists may have a LIVE session in it. Check ~/.claude/sessions/*.json before touching any tree. Verified today: sw-4 had a live session while looking idle from the outside.
4. Never remove a worktree that holds uncommitted changes, and never remove the session's own worktree.
5. Deletion is destructive, so default to REPORTING and require an explicit flag to act -- at least until the report has been trusted for a while.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: A command reports every branch and worktree fleet-wide with no unique commits vs origin/main, covering BOTH ai-cli-created worktrees and CC-native .claude/worktrees/agent-* trees.
AC-2: Deletion uses git's own safe delete and never force-deletes; a branch git considers unmerged is always refused and reported, never removed.
AC-3: Live sessions are detected via ~/.claude/sessions/*.json and their worktrees are never touched.
AC-4: Worktrees with uncommitted changes are never removed, and the session's own worktree is never removed.
AC-5: Reporting is the default; acting requires an explicit flag.
AC-6: The safety refusal is PROVEN able to fail -- demonstrate the command refusing a branch that holds unique work, not merely that it deleted the safe ones.
AC-7: Runs event-driven or scheduled per the fleet's preference for pub/sub over cron, and logs what it declined to touch and why.

title: Three canonical worktrees don't track origin/main — a sync check that reports 'in sync' while 46 commits behind
description:
Found 2026-07-27 during a fleet worktree sync. Audited the upstream of every canonical
`ai c` worktree (`<repo>/.worktrees/<name>` on `wt-<name>`) across the fleet. ~30 of them
correctly track `origin/main`. **Three do not:**

| worktree | upstream |
|---|---|
| `ai-ide-mobile/.worktrees/mobile-1` | `origin/wt-mobile-1` |
| `knowledge-curation/.worktrees/kc-1` | NONE |
| `ai-harness/.worktrees/aih-393-phase2` | NONE |

THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT "wrong upstream" — it is that a status check comes back TRUE AND USELESS.
`mobile-1` reported `ahead=0 behind=0` against its own upstream, i.e. perfectly in sync. Measured
against `origin/main` it was **0 ahead, 46 behind**. Both numbers were correct; only one of them
meant anything, and the reassuring one was the meaningless one.

That is the same shape as the inert gates this fleet removed five of on 2026-07-26: a check that
runs, passes, and cannot tell you the thing you actually needed to know. It also cost real
attention — a sweeping agent read the divergence backwards, reported `mobile-1` as "46 ahead of
origin/main… a parked/unmerged feature branch someone should look at", and skipped syncing it on
that basis. It held nothing unique. Driver re-measured after a fetch, confirmed 0 ahead / 46
behind, and fast-forwarded it (`--ff-only`, so no merge could be invented). It is now even.

The two NONE cases are the same defect in a milder form: with no upstream at all, `git status`
reports nothing about divergence, so those worktrees drift silently and no sync sweep can even
frame a question about them.

`kc-1` has a LIVE session in it as of this filing, so its tracking must not be changed out from
under that session.

STILL TO DECIDE (deliberately not done unilaterally — changing a branch's upstream is a config
change on someone else's working tree):
- Should every canonical worktree branch track `origin/main`, without exception? The fleet model
  says worktree branches track `origin/main` and commits ship straight to main, which implies yes,
  but `wt-mobile-1` having its own pushed remote branch suggests someone did it deliberately at
  some point.
- Whichever way that goes, the creation path should set it, so this cannot drift again.

WHERE THE FIX LIVES: `ai c` session-worktree creation is this repo's. `copier_update.py` and
`git_repair.py` both contain `worktree add` calls; the session launcher is the relevant one —
identify it before changing anything rather than patching the first match.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1 A newly created canonical worktree has the decided upstream set at creation time, verified by
     creating one and inspecting `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u}`.
AC-2 A check exists that distinguishes "in sync with upstream" from "in sync with origin/main", so
     a worktree cannot report healthy while 46 commits behind the branch that matters.
AC-3 AC-2's check is proven able to FAIL: point a scratch worktree at a non-main upstream, let it
     fall behind, and show the check flagging it. A check that passes on the current fleet proves
     nothing, since the current fleet is now clean.
AC-4 The three existing worktrees are dispositioned per the decision above; `kc-1` is not touched
     while a live session holds it.

title: ai-cli-utils: git_repair._git_env() guard applied to only 3 of 7 files doing cross-repo git targeting
description:
Found by the AIH-384 fleet sweep, 2026-07-26. This repo had the fleet's FIRST incident of the leaked-GIT_DIR class (AI-CLI-70) and built the correct shared fix — git_repair._git_env(). The fix was then applied to only some call sites.

Guarded: git_repair.py, session.py, copier_update.py (every -C/cwd= call passes env=_git_env()).

Unguarded, same vulnerable shape (cross-repo git with cwd=/-C, no env strip):
  - main.py:243,267,913,915,951,976 — NOTE main.py already imports _git_env at line 26 and uses it at 1459/1462/1464. The guard is literally in scope and just was not applied to these six.
  - workspace.py:28,33,38,44,95,97 — 'ai ws' is explicitly multi-repo, includes auto-stash/pull.
  - trust.py:72,156,166 — never imports _git_env; cross-repo by design (child param).
  - sync.py:979,985,992-1002 — _git_is_clean/_git_pull_rebase/_git_stash_pull_pop. Same file HAS a guarded _git() at L366 and a _GIT_ENV dict at L43; these three just do not use either. Docstring at L984 says 'Retained for direct library callers only' — possibly dead code, confirm before fixing.

CORRECTION to the sweep report, verified by the driver: it ranked main.py:915 'Highest' on the claim that its 'git pull --rebase --autostash' is what 'ai c N' runs at every session launch. It is NOT. Line 915 sits inside _do_update_or_deploy() (def at line 897) — that is 'ai update', updating ai-cli-utils itself, a far rarer path. Real risk is materially lower than the report states. Do not re-derive priority from that claim.

Nothing here is exploitable today: nothing invokes 'ai' from inside a live git hook. That is absence-of-wiring, not a structural guarantee — the same condition that made bd_roadmap_retire.py's gate silently inert.

Fix: route every cross-repo call through _git_env(), and add the AI-CLI-70-style regression test (decoy repo via GIT_DIR, assert correct targeting) verified to FAIL without the guard. title: Bug: long-running watchers leak zombie child processes (no SIGCHLD reaping)
description: `[P2]` `[AI-CLI-86]` **Bug: long-running watchers leak zombie child processes (no SIGCHLD reaping)** — FIXED 2026-07-04 (sw-3): reap the `ssh -f` tunnel parent in `messaging._reap_tunnel_parent` (poll, else bounded off-loop wait) on both tunnel-up and never-up paths; guarded `close()` terminate. Did NOT use SIGCHLD=SIG_IGN (watchers also run subprocess.run for git → ECHILD). 6 tunnel tests pass. Original scope: — Each long-running watcher (`ai internal signal-watch`, `ai sync watch`, `ai memory watch`) accumulates one persistent `<defunct>` child. Root cause: the NATS tunnel is spawned via `subprocess.Popen(["ssh", "-fN", ...])` in `messaging.py:71` and only ever `.terminate()`'d at shutdown (line 249) — never `.wait()`'d. `ssh -f` forks to background and the foreground process exits immediately after auth, but Python never reaps it, so it lingers as a zombie for the watcher's lifetime. No `SIGCHLD`/`SIG_IGN`/`waitpid` reaping exists anywhere in the codebase (`grep` confirmed). Harmless (empty proc-table slots, no memory/CPU) and self-clears when each session/watcher exits, but accumulates across live sessions. **Fix options:** (a) install `signal.signal(signal.SIGCHLD, signal.SIG_IGN)` at each watcher entrypoint (`_internal_signal_watch`, `cmd_sync_watch`, `cmd_memory_watch`) so the OS auto-reaps — general, one-liner each; or (b) `.wait()`/`.poll()` the tunnel `Popen` right after `ssh -f` returns (messaging-specific). Recommend (a). Note: takes effect only on watcher restart (i.e. new sessions); existing zombies cannot be reaped externally. Found during zombie-process cleanup 2026-07-03.

title: `ai copier-update` `--defaults` silently drops non-default stored copier answers
description: `[P2]` `[AI-CLI-92]` **`ai copier-update` `--defaults` silently drops non-default stored copier answers** — Filed 2026-07-06 (sw-1), found during the first fleet run of AI-CLI-91. `copier_update.py` invokes `copier update --defaults --trust --vcs-ref HEAD`. On **ai-harness** (which has `include_airflow: true`, a non-default answer), the run produced a `.copier-answers.yml` with `include_airflow` **removed entirely** — copier then treated it as the default (`false`) and proposed **deleting** ai-harness's live airflow infra (`.claude/hooks/airflow-watcher-*.sh`, `scripts/airflow-{trigger,watch}.sh`). The isolated flow correctly refused to auto-push it (flagged conflict), and it was resolved by hand (restored the files + the answer), but the root cause is the `--defaults` invocation re-defaulting **stored** answers, not just unanswered questions. **Impact:** narrow but real — any repo whose `.copier-answers.yml` holds a non-default value is at risk of a silent answer-reset (and destructive file removal) on `ai copier-update`. 17/19 repos were unaffected (their answers match defaults). **Fix:** research copier's `--defaults` semantics (does it re-default answered questions, or is `include_airflow` being seen as "new"?); switch to an invocation that preserves the existing answers file (e.g. drop `--defaults` and rely on `.copier-answers.yml`, or pass `--data-file`/`-A`), + a regression test that a non-default stored answer survives an update. Related: AI-CLI-91 (the tool), AIH-112 (aido §9 reconciliation from the same run). **UPDATE 2026-07-13 (aido-1):** the concrete airflow trigger is **gone** — AIH-110 (`ac1364c`) removed `include_airflow` + templated airflow from project-template entirely, so the specific "airflow-pin drop → script deletion" manifestation can no longer occur (aido **AIDO-193** was marked resolved/mooted on that basis; c-sw-4 verified `copier update --pretend` proposes no airflow deletion). **This task stays open** because the *general* defect — `copier update --defaults` re-defaulting **stored** non-default answers — is unproven-fixed and would still bite any *other* non-default `.copier-answers.yml` value. Reduced urgency (no known non-default answer remains across the fleet right now), but the `--defaults` invocation + a regression test (a non-default stored answer survives an update) are still the fix. Related: AIDO-193 (mooted airflow instance).

title: Worktree-isolated `ai copier-update` — run per-repo in an isolated worktree, resolve, merge to main, cleanup (safe while other sessions are active)
description: `[P2]` `[AI-CLI-91]` **Worktree-isolated `ai copier-update` — run per-repo in an isolated worktree, resolve, merge to main, cleanup (safe while other sessions are active)** — DONE 2026-07-06 (sw-1). Shipped: `copier_update.py` isolated flow (`_update_one_isolated` → temp worktree at `<repo>/.worktrees/copier-update` off `origin/main` → `copier update --vcs-ref HEAD` → on clean changes commit + push `HEAD:main` + rebase main tree + remove worktree; leaves the worktree in place only on CONFLICTS/PUSH FAILED). Isolated is the **default**; `--no-isolate` keeps the legacy direct-to-main-tree flow, `--no-push` commits without pushing. CLI flags wired in `main.py`; 35 copier tests (22 new, reproduction-first) + full suite 1754 green + ruff clean. Docs: `/copier-propagate` skill rewritten, `worktree-workflow.md` §Cross-repo-commits note, `ai-cli-reference.md` §Template-Propagation. Reinstalled 3 places (local Mac uv-tool, Hetzner uv-tool, aido venv). **Original spec below.** **Problem:** `ai copier-update` (`src/ai_cli/copier_update.py`) applies the template directly to each repo's **main working tree** and leaves uncommitted changes for a manual commit+push — which **clobbers/races any CC session actively working in that repo** (the main-tree / two-committers hazard; cf. AIH-48, the sw-4→ai-cli-utils incident). So fleet-wide propagation can't safely run while sessions are working (had to defer a reasoning-checkpoints propagation on 2026-07-06 for exactly this). **Fix (design, 2026-07-06):** for **each** target repo, `copier-update` should (1) create a temporary isolated **git worktree** off fresh `origin/main` (reuse `session.py::create_worktree`); (2) run `copier update` there; (3) **resolve rejections / `.rej` / merge conflicts** in the worktree (accept the new copier-answers commit hash, keep local project customizations — never discard project-specific content); (4) commit; (5) **merge → `main` + push** (personal repos: push `HEAD:main`; BMS: leave for PR); (6) **delete the temp worktree** (only if clean). Isolates all churn from active sessions → propagation becomes safe to run anytime. **Also update:** the `/copier-propagate` skill + `ai-harness/docs/procedures/worktree-workflow.md` to codify this as the standard, + the projects-wide config pointer. **Deliverable:** modified `copier_update.py` + reproduction-first tests + reinstall in 3 places (`feedback_aicli_deploy`: local Mac uv-tool, Hetzner uv-tool, aido venv). **Blocks:** safe fleet propagation of the canonical reasoning-checkpoints.md rule (in project-template `0e7d657`) — propagates once this ships, or on the next routine copier-update. Related: AI-CLI-89 (bare-root targeting — different, moot), AIH-48 (worktree model), AIH-89 (concurrent-worktree guardrails), AIH-101 (DB-ID allocation — same concurrent-safety theme).

title: `ai copier-update` must tolerate a relative `_src_path` in isolated-worktree mode
description: `[P2]` `[AI-CLI-107]` **`ai copier-update` must tolerate a relative `_src_path` in isolated-worktree mode** — Filed 2026-07-16 (Sergei, sw-4). During the AIH-174 fleet sweep, 3 repos (acn-automation, ai-cli-utils, aido) failed with copier's `Updating is only supported in git-tracked templates.` because their `.copier-answers.yml` had `_src_path: ../project-template` (a **relative** path). The wrapper runs `copier update` inside an isolated temp worktree (AI-CLI-91) whose CWD is NOT `~/projects/<repo>`, so `../project-template` resolves to a non-existent dir and copier can't see the template's git. Repos with a **URL** `_src_path` (`git@github.com:…`/`https://…`) work because copier clones fresh. **Two problems + fix:** (1) **Wrapper robustness (the fix):** before invoking copier in the temp worktree, resolve a relative `_src_path` to an absolute path (or the origin URL) — read it from the target repo's `.copier-answers.yml`, `os.path.realpath` it against the *original* repo dir, and pass it through so isolated mode works regardless of the stored form. (2) **Fleet convention drift:** `_src_path` is inconsistent across repos — some relative (`../project-template`), some `git@`, some `https://`; **pharma-lab-ai-platform was actively set back to local** (`e1a2a61`, another session) which re-broke its sweep. Decide a single canonical form (URL recommended — survives isolated mode + CWD-independent) and normalize the fleet, OR make (1) fully form-agnostic so it never matters. sw-4 hand-normalized the 3 blockers to `git@` URLs to unblock the AIH-174 sweep; this task is the durable fix. **Related:** AI-CLI-91 (isolated-worktree copier), AIH-174 (the sweep that surfaced it).

title: Escape literal dollar signs in docs per AIH-251 doc-authoring rule
description: An unescaped dollar sign in prose or a table cell is parsed as an inline-math delimiter by many markdown renderers (pandoc, GitHub, KaTeX/MathJax, the fleet PDF-export pipeline), silently italicizing everything between two unescaped dollar signs -- e.g. a dollar-amount range like 100 dollars through 200 dollars swallows the surrounding text into one italic math span. The convention (ai-harness projects-wide-session-config/rules/doc-authoring.md, AIH-251) is to escape every literal dollar sign with a backslash, except inside code fences and inline code spans (math is not parsed there) and except genuine intentional LaTeX math delimiters. A rough repo-wide grep found approximately 4 candidate files under docs/ in this repo -- this count is NOISY (it does not distinguish real prose dollar amounts from shell positional parameters inside code fences, which must NOT be touched) -- true scope requires per-file review respecting that exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: every literal dollar sign in prose/table-cell content under this repo's docs/ tree is escaped with a backslash, per the AIH-251 rule. AC-2: dollar signs inside code fences, inline code spans, and genuine intentional LaTeX math delimiters are left untouched -- verified by spot-checking a sample of fixed files. AC-3: a follow-up grep for un-escaped literal dollar-amount patterns outside code fences returns zero matches.

title: Research: should `ai c N` use Claude Code's native `EnterWorktree`/git-worktree mechanism instead of `ai cli`'s own separate worktree implementation?
description: `[P3]` `[AI-CLI-110]` **Research: should `ai c N` use Claude Code's native `EnterWorktree`/git-worktree mechanism instead of `ai cli`'s own separate worktree implementation?** — Filed 2026-07-18 (Sergei). `ai c N` currently creates `.worktrees/sw-N` on branch `wt-sw-N` itself (own git-plumbing, tracking `origin/main`, autostash pull etc). Claude Code CLI has since grown a native `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tool (creates a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`, `worktree.baseRef` setting for fresh-vs-head base). Investigate whether switching to (or wrapping) the native mechanism is worth it — pros: one less thing `ai cli` has to maintain/reinvent as CC's own worktree tooling evolves; cons: CC's native worktrees live under `.claude/worktrees/` with CC-chosen naming/branch conventions, not `.worktrees/sw-N` on `wt-sw-N` — need to confirm the native path can be configured/aliased to **still persist as a normal, directly-usable git worktree** (`git worktree list` visible, a real branch like `wt-sw-N`, survivable across CC restarts, not an ephemeral CC-managed-only construct) before this is viable; if it can't preserve that, don't switch. Exploratory — research first, no build committed yet. **Related:** the `ai c N` session-launcher (`docs/procedures/` or wherever its worktree logic lives), `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` CC tool docs.

title: Reconsider public-package-hygiene rule for internal docs
description: `[P3]` `[AI-CLI-119]` **Reconsider public-package-hygiene rule for internal docs** — Reconsider/relax the public-package-hygiene rule in this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` for internal planning docs (`docs/roadmap/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/audits/`, etc.) — Filed 2026-07-22 (Sergei, sw-1), surfaced by an AI-CLI-118 Round 1 `cx review` audit finding (F-4/AD-4): the plan doc under audit uses internal task IDs (`AI-CLI-N`, `AIH-N`) and the fleet's standard `Chosen (Sergei)` personal-name decision-tracking column, which literally conflicts with this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` ("no personal identifiers," "no private project names or prefixes," "all code, docs, comments, tests... written for a general audience"). This is **not unique to that one plan doc** — the same pattern (personal names, internal IDs) already runs throughout this repo's entire `docs/roadmap/master-roadmap.md` and other planning docs, so scrubbing just the one audited doc would be inconsistent without a broader policy call. **Confirmed low-stakes (Sergei, same session):** `pyproject.toml` ships only `packages = ["src/ai_cli"]` to PyPI — `docs/` is never part of the installable package, so this is a repo-visibility concern (GitHub browsability), not something that reaches end users of the published package. **Scope:** decide whether the public-package-hygiene rule should explicitly exempt internal planning docs (`docs/roadmap/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/audits/`, `docs/research/` — anything not shipped in the package and not primarily aimed at external contributors) while still applying in full to `src/`, `README.md`, and any user-facing docs; update `CLAUDE.md` accordingly if so. Not urgent — no one outside this fleet is currently reading or contributing to this repo. Related: AI-CLI-118 (the audit that surfaced this), the fleet's `ai-writing-anti-patterns.md`/outward-facing-writing convention this rule is downstream of.
