title: DONE 2026-07-13 (aido-1) — hermetic quota tests + pytest-randomly enabled (`d46632a`).
description: `[P3]` `[AI-CLI-97]` **DONE 2026-07-13 (aido-1) — hermetic quota tests + pytest-randomly enabled (`d46632a`).** Root-caused the flake to a **test-isolation breach** (not just an order-dep): quota/statusline tests touched **real user state** — `_get_quota_db_path()` fell back to the real `~/.local/state/ai-cli/quota.db` (live Fable data), and `_launch_background_scrape`/`_maybe_trigger_background_scrape` spawned a **real detached `ai quota scrape` subprocess** (20/30 `quota_statusline_part` tests didn't mock it) that writes the real DB + NATS KV; under xdist these race and inject real Fable data → the intermittent `F 🤖` vs `S 🤖`. **Fix:** conftest `_isolate_quota_state` autouse — redirect the quota DB to a per-test tmp + no-op the two scrape spawners; tests that exercise the spawners opt out via a new `real_quota_scrape` marker (they mock `subprocess.Popen` themselves). Regression tests assert DB-path isolation + no real spawn. **Verified 20/20 clean full `-n auto` + random-order runs** (was ~1-in-6 failing). `pytest-randomly` now locked in dev deps. Fed the broader finding into aido **AIDO-216** (ecosystem hermeticity audit). Original context follows. ~~Carry over AIDO-213 test-suite learnings — add `pytest-randomly`~~ (the one genuine gap; suite is otherwise already optimized)** — Filed 2026-07-13 (aido-1, from an AIDO-213 cross-repo review). Reviewed this suite against the aido test-perf work. **ai-cli-utils is already in good shape** and had independently applied aido's biggest levers: (1) **parallelized** — `pytest-xdist` + `addopts = "-n auto"` in `pyproject.toml`; (2) **the auto-reinstall/subprocess tail is already suppressed** — the conftest `_suppress_auto_update` autouse fixture patches `ai_cli.main._auto_update_if_stale`, which is the exact equivalent of aido's AIDO-213 T-a fix (aido's `_check_deps_and_auto_update` was firing a real `uv pip install -e` per test); (3) **arm64 venv** (no AIDO-214-style x86_64-on-arm64 corruption). Measured: **1771 tests in ~12.8s** parallel — already fast, not a slow suite. **The one transferable gap:** `pytest-randomly` is **not** installed (only `pytest-timeout` is) — this is aido's AIDO-213 **T-b**, a must-have per `sergei/docs/research/ai-native-testing-strategy.md` (randomized order surfaces hidden inter-test state). **TRIALED 2026-07-13 (aido-1) — pytest-randomly works and immediately did its job: it caught a REAL pre-existing order-dependency flake, so it is NOT yet enabled** (shipping it would make the pre-push gate intermittently RED; masking it would violate fix-first). **The flake:** `tests/test_quota.py::TestQuotaStatuslinePartAdaptiveLabels::test_wide_terminal_secondary_absent_uses_single_letter_label` — passes in isolation and in default order, but fails ~1-in-6 full-suite runs under `-n auto` + random order (renders the wide `Son` label instead of the `S` single-letter fallback when secondary data is absent). Root cause is a **within-worker module-state leak** (some earlier test on the same xdist worker leaves quota/statusline global state — candidate: `quota_db._DB_PATH_OVERRIDE` at `quota_db.py:66`, or a config/label cache read during rendering — that the failing test doesn't override). It is **rare + xdist-distribution-dependent, so not reproducible on-demand**, which is why it needs the quota-code owner (the ai-cli sessions that shipped AI-CLI-94/95/96) to fix + verify, not a blind aido-side patch. **This is now a 2-part task:** (1) **fix the leak at root cause** — the robust fix is an autouse conftest fixture that resets the leaked quota global(s) between tests (so it's leak-source-agnostic); confirm by looping the full `-n auto` suite ~20x green; (2) **then** `uv add --dev pytest-randomly` + wire it in. Low-risk once (1) lands. Review the aido design doc for the full rationale + the T-a root-cause pattern (in case a similar per-test subprocess cost ever appears here): [📄 aido/docs/designs/aido-213-test-suite-performance-followups.md](../../../aido/docs/designs/aido-213-test-suite-performance-followups.md) and the consolidated testing-perf research [📄 aido/docs/research/test-suite-performance-consolidation.md](../../../aido/docs/research/test-suite-performance-consolidation.md). **Secondary note:** if the pre-push gate ever *feels* slow, it's the pre-commit chain (markdownlint/ruff/shellcheck), not pytest — the tests themselves are ~13s. Related: AIDO-213 (source), AI-CLI-93 (Typer migration will touch the CLI tests).

title: Fix 6 pre-existing sync test failures on Windows (POSIX path encoding in `get_local_prefix`)
description: `[P3]` `[AI-CLI-101]` **Fix 6 pre-existing sync test failures on Windows (POSIX path encoding in `get_local_prefix`)** — Filed 2026-07-13 (acn-windows). `get_local_prefix()` encodes the home path via `re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "-", str(Path.home()))` — on Windows this yields `C--Users-...` instead of the POSIX `-Users-...` format that Claude Code actually produces. Six tests in `test_sync.py` create fake CC project directories using hardcoded POSIX-encoded names and fail on Windows: `test_replicate_history_to_worktrees_when_worktrees_exist_then_adds_entries`, `test_replicate_history_to_worktrees_when_verbose_then_prints`, `test_replicate_to_worktrees_when_matching_conv_then_replicates`, `test_purge_phantom_history_entries_when_verbose_then_prints`, `test_purge_phantom_history_entries_when_phantoms_exist_then_removes_them`, `test_sync_repos_when_worktree_bare_name_then_maps_to_base_project`. **Fix approach:** update test setup to call `get_local_prefix()` dynamically (or mock it to a fixed value) instead of hardcoding POSIX-format paths. **Fix on macOS/Hetzner** — sync is POSIX-centric (tmux, bare git, SSH); the canonical path format must be verified against what Claude Code actually produces on those systems.
